   321	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   322	class Finding:
   323	    """One observation, attributed to whoever owns the defect."""
   324	
   325	    kind: str  # "source" or "model"
   326	    source: str
   327	    detail: str
   328	
   329	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   330	        return {"kind": self.kind, "source": self.source, "detail": self.detail}
   331	
   332	
   333	@dataclass
   334	class CheckResult:
   335	    """Outcome of one named fidelity check."""
   336	
   337	    name: str
   338	    passed: bool
   339	    summary: str
   340	    failures: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   341	    source_findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)
   342	
   343	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   344	        return {
   345	            "check": self.name,
   346	            "passed": self.passed,
   347	            "summary": self.summary,
   348	            "failures": list(self.failures),
   349	            "sourceFindings": [finding.as_dict() for finding in self.source_findings],
   350	        }
   351	
   352	
   353	def _result(
   354	    name: str,
   355	    summary: str,
   356	    failures: Sequence[str],
   357	    source_findings: Sequence[Finding] = (),
   358	) -> CheckResult:
   359	    """Build a result whose ``passed`` is derived from its failures, never asserted."""
   360	    return CheckResult(
   361	        name=name,
   362	        passed=not failures,
   363	        summary=summary,
   364	        failures=list(failures),
   365	        source_findings=list(source_findings),
   366	    )
   367	
   368	
   369	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   370	# N-Quads reading: the Atlas side
   371	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   372	
   373	_ESCAPES = {"t": "\t", "b": "\b", "n": "\n", "r": "\r", "f": "\f", '"': '"', "'": "'", "\\": "\\"}
   374	
   375	
   376	def unescape_literal(raw: str) -> str:
   377	    """Decode an N-Triples literal body to the exact characters it denotes.
   378	
   379	    Byte fidelity is the whole point of this verifier, so this must be exact: a
   380	    label that differs from the publisher only by a decoded escape is identical,
   381	    and a label that differs by a real character is not.
   382	    """
   383	    out: list[str] = []
   384	    index = 0
   385	    length = len(raw)
   386	    while index < length:
   387	        char = raw[index]
   388	        if char != "\\":
   389	            out.append(char)
   390	            index += 1
   391	            continue
   392	        index += 1
   393	        if index >= length:
   394	            raise ValueError("truncated escape in literal")
   395	        marker = raw[index]
   396	        if marker in _ESCAPES:
   397	            out.append(_ESCAPES[marker])
   398	            index += 1
   399	        elif marker in ("u", "U"):
   400	            width = 4 if marker == "u" else 8
   401	            hex_digits = raw[index + 1 : index + 1 + width]
   402	            if len(hex_digits) != width:
   403	                raise ValueError(f"truncated \\{marker} escape in literal")
   404	            out.append(chr(int(hex_digits, 16)))
   405	            index += 1 + width
   406	        else:
   407	            raise ValueError(f"unknown escape \\{marker} in literal")
   408	    return "".join(out)
   409	
   410	
   411	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   412	class Quad:
   413	    """One losslessly parsed canonical N-Quads statement."""
   414	
   415	    subject: str
   416	    predicate: str
   417	    obj: str
   418	    is_literal: bool
   419	    language: str | None
   420	    datatype: str | None
   421	    graph: str
   422	
   423	
   424	_LITERAL_BODY = re.compile(r'^"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"(?:@([A-Za-z0-9-]+)|\^\^<([^>]*)>)?\s*$')
   425	
   426	
   427	def parse_nquads_line(line: str) -> Quad | None:
   428	    """Parse one canonical N-Quads line; return ``None`` for blanks and comments."""
   429	    stripped = line.strip()
   430	    if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
   431	        return None
   432	    if not stripped.endswith("."):
   433	        raise ValueError(f"N-Quads line does not terminate with '.': {stripped[:120]!r}")
   434	    body = stripped[:-1].strip()
   435	
   436	    if not body.startswith("<"):
   437	        raise ValueError(f"expected an IRI subject: {stripped[:120]!r}")
   438	    subject_end = body.index(">")
   439	    subject = body[1:subject_end]
   440	    rest = body[subject_end + 1 :].lstrip()
   441	
   442	    if not rest.startswith("<"):
   443	        raise ValueError(f"expected an IRI predicate: {stripped[:120]!r}")
   444	    predicate_end = rest.index(">")
   445	    predicate = rest[1:predicate_end]
   446	    rest = rest[predicate_end + 1 :].lstrip()
   447	
   448	    if rest.startswith("<"):
   449	        object_end = rest.index(">")
   450	        obj = rest[1:object_end]
   451	        graph = _graph_term(rest[object_end + 1 :], stripped)
   452	        return Quad(
   453	            subject,
   454	            predicate,
   455	            obj,
   456	            is_literal=False,
   457	            language=None,
   458	            datatype=None,
   459	            graph=graph,
   460	        )
   461	
   462	    if not rest.startswith('"'):
   463	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported object term: {stripped[:120]!r}")
   464	    closing = _closing_quote(rest)
   465	    literal_tail = rest[closing + 1 :].lstrip()
   466	    graph_start = _graph_start(literal_tail)
   467	    suffix = literal_tail[:graph_start].rstrip()
   468	    match = _LITERAL_BODY.match(rest[: closing + 1] + suffix)
   469	    if match is None:
   470	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported literal object: {stripped[:120]!r}")
   471	    graph = _graph_term(literal_tail[graph_start:], stripped)
   472	    return Quad(
   473	        subject,
   474	        predicate,
   475	        unescape_literal(match.group(1)),
   476	        is_literal=True,
   477	        language=match.group(2),
   478	        datatype=match.group(3),
   479	        graph=graph,
   480	    )
   481	
   482	
   483	def _closing_quote(text: str) -> int:
   484	    """Index of the quote that closes the literal opening at position 0."""
   485	    index = 1
   486	    while index < len(text):
   487	        if text[index] == "\\":
   488	            index += 2
   489	            continue
   490	        if text[index] == '"':
   491	            return index
   492	        index += 1
   493	    raise ValueError("unterminated literal")
   494	
   495	
   496	def _graph_start(tail: str) -> int:
   497	    """Return the start of the required graph IRI after a literal suffix."""
   498	    if tail.startswith("<"):
   499	        return 0
   500	    if tail.startswith("@"):
   501	        marker = tail.find(" <")
   502	        if marker >= 0:
   503	            return marker + 1
   504	    if tail.startswith("^^<"):
   505	        datatype_end = tail.find(">")
   506	        if datatype_end >= 0:
   507	            marker = tail.find("<", datatype_end + 1)
   508	            if marker >= 0:
   509	                return marker
   510	    raise ValueError(f"literal has no graph IRI: {tail[:120]!r}")
   511	
   512	
   513	def _graph_term(tail: str, line: str) -> str:
   514	    """Parse a graph IRI and reject unconsumed terms."""
   515	    text = tail.strip()
   516	    if not text.startswith("<") or not text.endswith(">") or text.count("<") != 1:
   517	        raise ValueError(f"invalid or missing graph IRI: {line[:120]!r}")
   518	    return text[1:-1]
   519	
   520	
   521	def read_pack(
   522	    path: Path,
   523	    failures: list[str] | None = None,
   524	    observations: dict[str, tuple[str, int]] | None = None,
   525	    logical_path: str | None = None,
   526	) -> Iterator[Quad]:
   527	    """Parse one immutable pack snapshot and retain its actual transport identity."""
   528	    payload = path.read_bytes()
   529	    if observations is not None:
   530	        observations[logical_path or path.as_posix()] = (
   531	            "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
   532	            len(payload),
   533	        )
   534	    with zstd.open(io.BytesIO(payload), "rt", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   535	        for number, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
   536	            try:
   537	                quad = parse_nquads_line(line)
   538	            except ValueError as error:
   539	                detail = f"{path.name}:{number}: {error}"
   540	                if failures is None:
   541	                    raise ValueError(detail) from error
   542	                failures.append(detail)
   543	                continue
   544	            if quad is not None:
   545	                yield quad
   546

   553	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   554	class LiteralValue:
   555	    """One literal with the language and datatype needed to detect silent rewrites."""
   556	
   557	    value: str
   558	    language: str | None
   559	    datatype: str | None
   560	
   561	
   562	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   563	class ReifiedStatement:
   564	    """One exact RDF reification row from publisher bytes."""
   565	
   566	    statement_iri: str
   567	    subject_iri: str
   568	    predicate_iri: str
   569	    object_iri: str | None = None
   570	    object_literal: LiteralValue | None = None
   571	
   572	
   573	def _literal_value(value: str, language: str | None, datatype: str | None) -> LiteralValue:
   574	    """Represent the RDF 1.1 datatype of a plain literal explicitly."""
   575	    if language is None and datatype is None:
   576	        datatype = f"{XSD}string"
   577	    return LiteralValue(value, language, datatype)
   578	
   579	
   580	def _literal_repr(literal: LiteralValue) -> str:
   581	    """Render one literal with the tag or datatype that makes a rewrite visible."""
   582	    if literal.language is not None:
   583	        return f"{literal.value!r}@{literal.language}"
   584	    return f"{literal.value!r}^^<{literal.datatype}>"

   110	# The lifecycle-event class is rkaf:LifecycleEvent. Its event kind, effective
   111	# date, and subject are rkaf's too; see atlas:LifecycleEventShape in
   112	# shapes/atlas.shacl.ttl, which closes the kind to the two kernel kinds Atlas
   113	# can justify. Only the two release pointers below stay Atlas-owned, because a
   114	# release is structure RefSpec owns.
   115	
   116	# MACHINE ADJUDICATION -- five more adopted rkaf classes, no atlas: term at all.
   117	#
   118	# Atlas 1.0 carried a private protocol for machine-qualified mappings:
   119	# atlas:MachineValidation, atlas:verdictRelation, atlas:adjudicatedRelation,
   120	# atlas:qualifiedBy, atlas:requestArtifact, atlas:inputContextArtifact /
   121	# atlas:inputContextDigest. Rulespec now owns every one of those semantics
   122	# (constraints/analysis/resolver-proof-record.cue, machine-adjudication.cue,
   123	# relation-comparison-context.cue, constraints/core/{ai-lineage,artifact}.cue),
   124	# so Atlas 3.1 publishes rkaf's records rather than a second name for them, and
   125	# mints nothing of its own here:
   126	#
   127	#   rkaf:ResolverProofRecord        one machine's sealed, reviewable answer to
   128	#                                   one comparison question -- was
   129	#                                   atlas:MachineValidation. Narrowed by
   130	#                                   rkaf:proofType, never by a second rdf:type,
   131	#                                   exactly as machine-adjudication.cue
   132	#                                   requires; #MachineAdjudicationProof is that
   133	#                                   narrowing, not a second wire class.
   134	#   rkaf:ResolverProofIssuer        the versioned resolver and policy a proof
   135	#                                   was issued under. The independence axes
   136	#                                   "validator actor" and "provider" are read
   137	#                                   here (the issuer IRI, and its
   138	#                                   rkaf:proofResolver) rather than copied onto
   139	#                                   every proof.
   140	#   rkaf:AILineage                  which model answered, at which version,
   141	#                                   under which prompt contract and sampling
   142	#                                   settings, over which input context. The
   143	#                                   "provider model id" axis is
   144	#                                   rkaf:hasAILineage -> rkaf:modelId.
   145	#   rkaf:Artifact                   an immutable state with a content digest.
   146	#                                   Four per comparison: the two compared
   147	#                                   endpoints, the sealed request, and one
   148	#                                   sealed response per proof -- was
   149	#                                   atlas:inputContextArtifact plus
   150	#                                   atlas:requestArtifact and the sealed
   151	#                                   response artifact.
   152	#   rkaf:RelationComparisonContext  the comparison itself: the artifact pair,
   153	#                                   which Atlas assertion it was run for, its
   154	#                                   outcome, and the COMPLETE set of proofs
   155	#                                   that supported it -- was atlas:qualifiedBy
   156	#                                   on the mapping.
   157	#
   158	# Three v1 -> rkaf mapping decisions are recorded here because nothing else on
   159	# the wire records them:
   160	#
   161	# 1. THE VERDICT ENUM LOSES TWO VALUES, AND THE OUTCOME ENUM GAINS THEM BACK.
   162	#    v1's atlas:verdictRelation had seven (same, near_same, target_is_broader,
   163	#    target_is_narrower, related, unrelated, insufficient_evidence). rkaf's
   164	#    #MachineAdjudicationVerdict has five: a verdict NAMES A RELATION, and
   165	#    "unrelated" and "insufficient_evidence" name no relation -- they are
   166	#    refusals, and a refusal is a gate result. On the v3 wire a refusal rides in
   167	#    rkaf:proofOutcome (rkaf:gateFail for a refused comparison,
   168	#    rkaf:gateUnknown for one nobody could decide), and the comparison carrying
   169	#    it takes one of the four non-satisfied #RelationComparisonOutcome values.
   170	#    Atlas PUBLISHES those records rather than pinning them away: a consumer
   171	#    that cannot tell "never adjudicated" from "adjudicated and refused" has
   172	#    lost exactly the distinction relation-comparison-context.cue keeps five
   173	#    outcomes to preserve. Licensing stays strict and lives in validate.py.
   174	#
   175	# 2. atlas:adjudicatedRelation AND atlas:qualifiedBy BOTH DISAPPEAR, and
   176	#    neither is replaced by an atlas: term. The adjudicated relation is the
   177	#    mapping assertion's own rdf:predicate -- v1 needed a separate field only
   178	#    because its candidate record was not yet an assertion, and a second copy
   179	#    of the relation could only agree or disagree with the one the mapping
   180	#    already states (the same argument that deleted atlas:assertionStatus).
   181	#    The proof set is rkaf:comparisonProofRecord on the comparison, and the
   182	#    link from the Atlas mapping record to its comparison is
   183	#    rkaf:comparisonExpectedAssertion pointing the other way -- "the baseline
   184	#    assertion the comparison was run for", which is exactly the fact an
   185	#    atlas: link property would have minted. rkaf has the term; Atlas uses it.
   186	#
   187	# 3. atlas:reason BECOMES rkaf:proofRationale, AND STAYS NON-AUTHORITATIVE.
   188	#    v1 carried the model's free text as atlas:reason and said a consumer MUST
   189	#    NOT treat it as evidence, because nothing tied the literal to the sealed
   190	#    response it quoted. Dropping the field was the wrong fix: upstream requires
   191	#    a rationale on every proof, for the good reason that a decision with no
   192	#    stated reason is not reviewable. So the field is carried under rkaf's name
   193	#    and the v1 caveat is answered rather than deleted -- the authoritative text
   194	#    is the rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact, which this binding resolves to bundled
   195	#    bytes. A consumer reads rkaf:proofRationale to see why a machine decided as
   196	#    it did, and the sealed response artifact when it needs what was returned.
   197	#
   198	# Every field each of the five classes requires upstream is on the wire; the
   199	# shapes are sh:closed, and a closed shape missing a required upstream field
   200	# would both accept records rulespec rejects and reject records rulespec
   201	# requires. Upstream's optional fields Atlas does not use are simply absent,
   202	# and the two it requires anyway (rkaf:proofInputDigest, rkaf:hasContentDigest)
   203	# are narrowing, which a binding profile may do.
   204	#
   205	# The cross-node rules -- at least one independent pair on five axes, one
   206	# sealed question per comparison, complete support retained, the verdict
   207	# lattice, the snapshot chain, and the resolution of every artifact and digest
   208	# to bundled bytes -- are in bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py, not here and
   209	# not in the SHACL, for the reason rulespec gives: they relate several proof
   210	# records to one comparison, and per-property SHACL constrains one node.
   211	
   212	# RING TEMPORAL CONTEXT -- one more adopted rkaf class, and one atlas: term
   213	# deliberately NOT minted.
   214	#
   215	# A crosswalk between two code editions and a legal-identity equivalence are
   216	# both claims about a period, not about all time: "these two codes mean the
   217	# same thing from 2022-01-01" is a different assertion from "these two codes
   218	# mean the same thing". The registry has enforced that since it had rings --
   219	# src/refspec/registry/infrastructure/semantic_foundation.py requires a
   220	# value-ring and a legal-identity mapping to carry effective dates and refuses
   221	# them on the other two -- but none of it reached the wire, so a consumer reading
   222	# the published Atlas could not tell a dated crosswalk from an undated one.
   223	#
   224	#   rkaf:EffectivePeriod           the period itself, upstream's own record for
   225	#                                  it (constraints/core/effective-period.cue),
   226	#                                  reached through rkaf:hasEffectivePeriod and
   227	#                                  carrying rkaf:effectivePeriodStart and the
   228	#                                  optional rkaf:effectivePeriodEnd. Atlas
   229	#                                  publishes those two fields; upstream's other
   230	#                                  two optional fields, rkaf:retroactiveFrom and
   231	#                                  rkaf:sunsetAt, are absent, which is what an
   232	#                                  optional field means -- Atlas has no producer
   233	#                                  for either, and a field nothing writes and
   234	#                                  nothing checks is how atlas:eventType got
   235	#                                  into the state that deleted it.
   236	#
   237	# The same predicate already names the RELEASE-level period upstream
   238	# (reference-resource-release.cue:42), which src/refspec/atlas/model.py folds
   239	# into the closed digest preimage of an rkaf:ReferenceResourceRelease. That is
   240	# a sibling use of one rkaf term on a different subject, not a second term:
   241	# rkaf reuses rkaf:hasEffectivePeriod on four upstream shapes for exactly this
   242	# reason, and attestation.cue records the rule -- domain expansion, not a
   243	# parallel predicate. Atlas follows it.
   244	#
   245	# TWO MAPPING DECISIONS, recorded here because nothing else on the wire records
   246	# them:
   247	#
   248	# 1. NO EDITION LITERAL, ON EITHER SIDE. Minting atlas:sourceEdition and
   249	#    atlas:targetEdition here would be legal -- neither local name is rkaf's --
   250	#    and it would be the atlas:assertionStatus mistake again. An edition of a
   251	#    scheme IS an atlas:AtlasRelease: the release IRIs the real registry emits
   252	#    are the editions (urn:ref:atlas-release:3:eurovoc:4.24, :elsst:r6,
   253	#    :doe-osti-thesaurus:v1-2020, and the content-digest-keyed form in
   254	#    src/refspec/atlas/v3_registry_codes.py), a second capture of one scheme at
   255	#    a different edition is necessarily a different release node, and every
   256	#    mapping already pins both: atlas:sourceRelease and atlas:targetRelease,
   257	#    each SHACL-equal to its endpoint's own atlas:inRelease
   258	#    (atlas:MappingAssertionShape, negative case mapping-wrong-endpoint-release).
   259	#    An edition literal beside them could only agree or disagree with the pin,
   260	#    and disagreement is the only thing it could ever be checked for. What the

   713	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   714	class SourceExtractSelector:
   715	    """One non-RDF publisher artifact compared through its checked-in extract.
   716	
   717	    Some publishers ship no machine-readable distribution at all -- the Federal
   718	    Register thesaurus is a styled PDF. For those releases the comparison basis
   719	    is the repository-checked semantic extract of the pinned artifact: bytes
   720	    that live in git, are pinned here by digest, are *not* read by the builder
   721	    (which re-parses the PDF on every build), and whose own header binds the
   722	    exact publisher artifact this comparison authenticates.
   723	
   724	    This is weaker than the RDF comparisons and says so in the receipt: it is
   725	    not an independent re-parse of the publisher's bytes, it is a frozen
   726	    re-statement of them. What it does catch is every drift between what the
   727	    builder parsed out of the pinned artifact and what git recorded.
   728	    """
   729	
   730	    reader: str
   731	    extract: SourcePin
   732	    source_release_iri: str
   733	    label_language: str
   734	    relation_predicate: str

   761	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   762	class DeclaredClaimExclusion:
   763	    """One publisher entity layer a release declares Atlas does not represent.
   764	
   765	    This is a claim-scope declaration, never a waiver. Some publishers ship
   766	    entity kinds beside their terms -- GEMET's Group/Theme/SuperGroup
   767	    collections and its bibliographic Source register, the Publications Office's
   768	    void/lime dataset descriptions -- that Atlas deliberately does not model.
   769	    Leaving those claims in the uncovered report says "we have not looked yet",
   770	    which is false; dropping them silently is worse. An exclusion says instead:
   771	    here is the exact subject set, here is every claim it covers counted by
   772	    predicate, and here is the paired assertion that Atlas asserts *nothing*
   773	    about any of those subjects.
   774	
   775	    That pairing is what keeps it fail-closed. The exclusion only ever removes
   776	    publisher claims from the residue; the Atlas side of the same subjects stays
   777	    in the comparison, so one manufactured claim about an excluded subject fails
   778	    both ``source-claim-coverage`` and ``claim-scope``. An exclusion that
   779	    overlaps a subject the comparison actually compares is itself a failure.
   780	
   781	    Subjects are selected by declared rdf:type or by IRI prefix -- both
   782	    enumerable from the publisher's own bytes, so the receipt can print the set.
   783	    """
   784	
   785	    name: str
   786	    reason: str
   787	    subject_types: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
   788	    subject_iri_prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
   789	
   790	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
   791	        if not self.subject_types and not self.subject_iri_prefixes:
   792	            raise ValueError(
   793	                f"declared claim exclusion {self.name!r} selects no subjects; an "
   794	                "exclusion must name the exact subject set it covers"
   795	            )
   796	
   797	    def selects(self, subject: str, types: frozenset[str]) -> bool:
   798	        """Return whether one publisher subject falls inside this declaration."""
   799	        if self.subject_types & types:
   800	            return True
   801	        return bool(self.subject_iri_prefixes) and subject.startswith(
   802	            self.subject_iri_prefixes
   803	        )
   804	
   805	
   806	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   807	class SourceSpec:
   808	    """One source vocabulary the verifier knows how to compare end to end."""
   809	
   810	    name: str
   811	    kind: str  # "vocabulary", "mapping", "native-control", or "source-extract"
   812	    release_keys: tuple[str, ...]
   813	    inputs: tuple[SourcePin, ...]
   814	    policies: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
   815	    subset: str = "all"
   816	    included_concept_iris: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
   817	    excluded_resource_predicates: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
   818	    declared_claim_exclusions: tuple[DeclaredClaimExclusion, ...] = ()
   819	    native_control: NativeControlSelector | None = None
   820	    rdf_source: RdfSourcePolicy | None = None
   821	    source_extract: SourceExtractSelector | None = None
   822	
   823	    def has_policy(self, name: str) -> bool:
   824	        return name in self.policies
   825	
   826

   829	    """A publisher view and the Atlas view that claims to represent it."""
   830	
   831	    spec: SourceSpec
   832	    publisher: PublisherView
   833	    atlas: AtlasView

  3120	            control_id=control_id,

  3138	    evaluated_native_payload_fields: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
  3139	    *,
  3140	    atlas_only_native_payload_fields: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
  3141	    additional_annotation_predicates: tuple[str, ...] = (),
  3142	    additional_relation_predicates: tuple[str, ...] = (),
  3143	    label_language_inverse: str = "english-tagged",
  3144	    literal_reification_id_rules: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = (),
  3145	    note_predicate_inverse: str | None = None,
  3146	    reification_base_iri: str | None = None,
  3147	    reification_predicates: tuple[str, ...] = (),
  3148	    reification_weight_predicate: str | None = None,
  3149	    reification_weight_value: LiteralValue | None = None,
  3150	    relation_predicate_inverse: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (),
  3151	    relation_scope: str = "member-subject",
  3152	    source_wide_literal_predicates: tuple[str, ...] = (),
  3153	    record_digest_input_paths: tuple[str, ...] = (),
  3154	    record_locator: str | None = None,
  3155	    record_input_path_by_resource: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (),
  3156	    record_locator_by_resource: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (),
  3157	) -> RdfSourcePolicy:
  3158	    """Declare only the publisher-evidence fields one RDF adapter reverses."""
  3159	    return RdfSourcePolicy(
  3160	        evaluated_native_payload_fields=evaluated_native_payload_fields,

  3170	        reification_weight_value=reification_weight_value,
  3171	        relation_predicate_inverse=relation_predicate_inverse,
  3172	        relation_scope=relation_scope,

  3176	        record_input_path_by_resource=record_input_path_by_resource,
  3177	        record_locator_by_resource=record_locator_by_resource,
  3178	    )

  6913	def _publisher_subject_types(view: PublisherView) -> dict[str, frozenset[str]]:
  6914	    """Index the rdf:type values the publisher's own bytes assert per subject."""
  6915	    types: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
  6916	    for subject, predicate, obj in view.iri_claims:
  6917	        if predicate == RDF_TYPE:
  6918	            types[subject].add(obj)
  6919	    return {subject: frozenset(values) for subject, values in types.items()}
  6920	
  6921	
  6922	def _compared_publisher_subjects(pair: SourcePair) -> frozenset[str]:
  6923	    """Return the publisher subjects this adapter's comparisons actually read.
  6924	
  6925	    A declared exclusion that touches one of these would be hiding a compared
  6926	    claim behind a scope declaration, so this is what the overlap guard tests.
  6927	    """
  6928	    endpoints = {
  6929	        *(subject for subject, _, _ in pair.publisher.relations),
  6930	        *(obj for _, _, obj in pair.publisher.relations),
  6931	    }
  6932	    if pair.spec.kind == "mapping":
  6933	        return frozenset(endpoints)
  6934	    return frozenset(
  6935	        {
  6936	            *endpoints,
  6937	            *pair.publisher.concepts,
  6938	            *_publisher_source_scheme_subjects(pair.publisher),
  6939	            *pair.publisher.resource_annotation_target_claim_counts,
  6940	        }
  6941	    )
  6942	
  6943	
  6944	def _declared_exclusion_subjects(
  6945	    pair: SourcePair,
  6946	) -> tuple[tuple[DeclaredClaimExclusion, frozenset[str]], ...]:
  6947	    """Resolve each declared exclusion to the exact publisher subjects it selects."""
  6948	    exclusions = pair.spec.declared_claim_exclusions
  6949	    if not exclusions:
  6950	        return ()
  6951	    types = _publisher_subject_types(pair.publisher)
  6952	    subjects = {
  6953	        *(subject for subject, _, _ in pair.publisher.iri_claims),
  6954	        *(subject for subject, _, _ in pair.publisher.literal_claims),
  6955	    }
  6956	    resolved: list[tuple[DeclaredClaimExclusion, frozenset[str]]] = []
  6957	    for exclusion in exclusions:
  6958	        empty: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
  6959	        resolved.append(
  6960	            (
  6961	                exclusion,
  6962	                frozenset(
  6963	                    subject
  6964	                    for subject in subjects
  6965	                    if exclusion.selects(subject, types.get(subject, empty))
  6966	                ),
  6967	            )
  6968	        )
  6969	    return tuple(resolved)
  6970	
  6971	
  6972	def _declared_excluded_publisher_claims(
  6973	    pair: SourcePair,
  6974	) -> tuple[
  6975	    frozenset[tuple[str, str, str]],
  6976	    frozenset[tuple[str, str, LiteralValue]],
  6977	]:
  6978	    """Return the publisher claims every declared exclusion accounts for.
  6979	
  6980	    Subjects the comparison actually compares are never excluded, whatever a
  6981	    declaration says: the overlap is reported as a failure by ``claim-scope``
  6982	    instead of quietly shrinking the residue.
  6983	    """
  6984	    resolved = _declared_exclusion_subjects(pair)
  6985	    if not resolved:
  6986	        return frozenset(), frozenset()
  6987	    compared = _compared_publisher_subjects(pair)
  6988	    selected = frozenset().union(*(subjects for _, subjects in resolved)) - compared
  6989	    return (
  6990	        frozenset(row for row in pair.publisher.iri_claims if row[0] in selected),
  6991	        frozenset(row for row in pair.publisher.literal_claims if row[0] in selected),
  6992	    )
  6993	
  6994	
  6995	def _declared_claim_exclusion_report(pair: SourcePair) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
  6996	    """Report each declared exclusion, what it covers, and whether it still holds."""
  6997	    resolved = _declared_exclusion_subjects(pair)
  6998	    if not resolved:
  6999	        return []
  7000	    compared = _compared_publisher_subjects(pair)
  7001	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
  7002	    for exclusion, subjects in resolved:
  7003	        overlap = sorted(subjects & compared)
  7004	        selected = subjects - compared
  7005	        counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
  7006	        for subject, predicate, _ in pair.publisher.iri_claims:
  7007	            if subject in selected:
  7008	                counts[predicate] += 1
  7009	        for subject, predicate, _ in pair.publisher.literal_claims:
  7010	            if subject in selected:
  7011	                counts[predicate] += 1
  7012	        atlas_iri = sorted(
  7013	            row for row in pair.atlas.all_raw_iri_claims if row[0] in selected
  7014	        )
  7015	        atlas_literals = sorted(
  7016	            (row for row in pair.atlas.all_raw_literal_claims if row[0] in selected),
  7017	            key=_literal_claim_sort_key,
  7018	        )
  7019	        atlas_claims = [
  7020	            *(list(row) for row in atlas_iri[:5]),
  7021	            *(
  7022	                [subject, predicate, _literal_repr(literal)]
  7023	                for subject, predicate, literal in atlas_literals[:5]
  7024	            ),
  7025	        ]
  7026	        blank_node_claims = pair.publisher.declared_out_of_scope_blank_node_claims.get(
  7027	            exclusion.name, ()
  7028	        )
  7029	        holds = not atlas_iri and not atlas_literals and not overlap
  7030	        rows.append(
  7031	            {
  7032	                "name": exclusion.name,
  7033	                "reason": exclusion.reason,
  7034	                "subjectTypes": sorted(exclusion.subject_types),
  7035	                "subjectIriPrefixes": list(exclusion.subject_iri_prefixes),
  8560	            "note": (
  8561	                "the publisher ships a styled PDF; the comparison basis is the "
  8562	                "repository-checked semantic extract of the authenticated artifact, "
  8563	                "which the builder does not read"
  8564	            ),
  8565	        },
  8566	    }

  8569	def _cached_comparison_claim_scope(
  8570	    ctx: Context,
  8571	    spec: SourceSpec,
  8572	    pair: SourcePair | None,
  8573	) -> dict[str, Any]:
  8574	    """Compute one immutable-input claim scope once and reuse it in the receipt."""
  8575	    cached = ctx.comparison_claim_scope_cache.get(spec)
  8576	    if cached is not None:
  8577	        return cached
  8578	    scope = _comparison_claim_scope(spec, pair)
  8579	    ctx.comparison_claim_scope_cache[spec] = scope
  8580	    return scope

  8583	def _evaluate_claim_scope(ctx: Context) -> CheckResult:
  8584	    """Fail closed on unhandled publisher predicates or known lossy representations."""
  8585	    failures = _incomplete_evaluation_failure(ctx, "claim-scope review")

  8595	            failures.append(

  8598	            )

  8608	                )
  8609	            if family["comparedSubjectOverlapCount"]:
  8610	                failures.append(
  8611	                    f"{pair.spec.name}: declared exclusion {family['name']} covers "
  8612	                    f"{family['comparedSubjectOverlapCount']} subject(s) this "
  8613	                    "comparison also compares; a scope declaration may never hide a "
  8614	                    f"compared claim; examples {family['comparedSubjectOverlapExamples']}"
  8615	                )

  8618	                failures.append(
  8619	                    f"{pair.spec.name}: {family['name']} is represented with known semantic loss"
  8620	                )
  8621	            elif family["status"] not in {"exact", "not-applicable"}:
  8622	                failures.append(
  8623	                    f"{pair.spec.name}: {family['name']} source claims are "
  8624	                    f"{family['status']}"
  8625	                )

  8631	        ]

  8633	        checked += len(scope["claimFamilies"])

   431	def _notes(graph: Graph) -> tuple[AgrovocNote, ...]:
   432	    notes: list[AgrovocNote] = []
   433	    for predicate_iri in NOTE_PREDICATE_IRIS:
   434	        predicate = URIRef(predicate_iri)
   435	        for subject, value in graph.subject_objects(predicate):
   436	            notes.append(
   437	                AgrovocNote(
   438	                    subject_iri=_iri(subject, "note subject"),
   439	                    property_iri=predicate_iri,

   441	                )
   442	            )
   443	    return tuple(
   444	        sorted(
   445	            notes,
   446	            key=lambda item: (
   447	                item.subject_iri,

   450	                item.value.lexical_form,

   452	            ),
   453	        )

   281	            concepts=len(self.concepts),
   282	            concept_schemes=len(self.concept_schemes),
   283	            preferred_labels=labels["preferred"],
   284	            alternate_labels=labels["alternate"],
   285	            hidden_labels=labels["hidden"],
   286	            notes=len(self.notes),

   288	            broader_relations=semantics[BROADER_PREDICATE_IRI],
   289	            narrower_relations=semantics[NARROWER_PREDICATE_IRI],
   290	            related_relations=semantics[RELATED_PREDICATE_IRI],
   291	            deprecated_assertions=len(self.deprecated_assertions),

   300	        )

   403	                item.property_iri,
   404	                item.value.language_tag or "",

   406	                item.value.datatype_iri or "",
   407	            ),
   408	        )
   409	    )

   412	def _notes(graph: Graph) -> tuple[ElsstNote, ...]:
   413	    notes: list[ElsstNote] = []
   414	    for predicate_iri in ELSST_NOTE_PREDICATE_IRIS:
   415	        predicate = URIRef(predicate_iri)
   416	        for subject, value in graph.subject_objects(predicate):
   417	            notes.append(
   418	                ElsstNote(
   419	                    subject_iri=_iri(subject, "note subject"),

   421	                    value=_literal(value, f"{predicate_iri} value"),
   422	                )
   423	            )
   424	    return tuple(
   425	        sorted(
   426	            notes,
   427	            key=lambda item: (
   428	                item.subject_iri,
   429	                item.property_iri,
   430	                item.value.language_tag or "",
   431	                item.value.lexical_form,
   432	                item.value.datatype_iri or "",
   433	            ),
   434	        )
   435	    )

     1	"""Source-faithful capture of the DOE OSTI Semantic Thesaurus 2020 RDF/SKOS export.
     2	
     3	Source: DOE Data Explorer dataset record
     4	https://www.osti.gov/dataexplorer/biblio/dataset/1668761 (OSTI identifier
     5	1668761, DOI https://doi.org/10.11578/1668761), "OSTI Semantic Thesaurus v1",
     6	publication date stated as 2020-09-30. The record's own abstract states: "This
     7	dataset is an export from the OSTI Semantic Thesaurus in RDF/SKOS format...
     8	While the full thesaurus includes additional relation types which may be
     9	included in future revisions, this export is limited to broader, narrower,
    10	and related term relations. Definitions and scope notes are included where
    11	available." The distribution file itself was verified 2026-08-03 by
    12	downloading https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1668761 (18,087,998 bytes,
    13	sha256:aeb9fb2d16caff675c7c9e12e0baff04ac4aded07488944acdf73ed859abe1d5) --
    14	this module's pinned digest and byte length for ``DOE_OSTI_THESAURUS_V1_2020``
    15	are the exact result of that verified capture, not a guess.
    16	
    17	Catalog scope (binding): the 2026-07-28 catalog recorded this as a "Public
    18	2020 Resource Description Framework/SKOS artifact; no newer public release or
    19	changelog was verified", specialist role "Energy/science mapping research",
    20	decision "Reject/defer canonical use until the owner provides a current,
    21	licensed, reproducible release." The importing agent's guidance frames this as
    22	a best-in-category inclusion -- nothing newer exists for energy/physical
    23	science -- to be imported "with the staleness recorded prominently in package
    24	metadata," in a mapping/research role, not as a governed current authority.
    25	This module captures a real, verified 2020 export and keeps every staleness
    26	and license verification gap explicit (``DOE_OSTI_THESAURUS_VERIFICATION_GAPS``)
    27	rather than resolving or hiding them. The capture carries no permission
    28	fields; exact product policy governs use.
    29	
    30	Source shape (verified against the real 2020-09-30 distribution): a single
    31	``<rdf:RDF>`` document holding one ``skos:ConceptScheme`` (IRI
    32	``https://www.osti.gov/thesaurus``) and 23,626 ``skos:Concept`` elements. Every
    33	literal in the verified distribution carries only an "en" language tag; there
    34	is no ``skos:altLabel``, ``skos:hiddenLabel``, ``skos:notation``, no
    35	``skos:*Match`` mapping relation, and no ``dcterms:*`` metadata embedded in
    36	the graph at all (the 2020-09-30 publication date lives only in the Data
    37	Explorer record, never in the RDF itself). Concept identifiers are the
    38	publisher's own numeric thesaurus IRIs (for example
    39	``https://www.osti.gov/thesaurus/3792``); per house rule this module reuses
    40	those IRIs exactly and never mints a concept identity of its own. Because the
    41	abstract itself warns that "the full thesaurus includes additional relation
    42	types which may be included in future revisions," the parser refuses any
    43	predicate outside its fixed allow-list instead of silently accepting or
    44	dropping an unverified shape change.
    45	
    46	Importing this module never opens a network connection. A caller must either
    47	supply already-fetched bytes or inject a fetcher; direct network access
    48	requires the caller to opt in explicitly.
    49	"""

   239	def _require_absolute_iri(value: str, label: str) -> str:
   240	    if not urllib.parse.urlsplit(value).scheme:
   241	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(f"{label} must be an absolute IRI, got {value!r}")
   242	    return value
   243	
   244	
   245	def _validate_source_url(value: str) -> None:
   246	    parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(value)
   247	    if parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https"} or not parsed.netloc:
   248	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError("source_url must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL")
   249	    if parsed.username is not None or parsed.password is not None:
   250	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError("source_url must not contain credentials")
   251	
   252	
   253	def _expected_hex(expected_sha256: str) -> str:
   254	    if not expected_sha256.startswith(_DIGEST_PREFIX) or len(expected_sha256) != len(_DIGEST_PREFIX) + 64:
   255	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError("expected_sha256 must be a lowercase sha256:<64 hex> digest")
   256	    hex_part = expected_sha256[len(_DIGEST_PREFIX) :]
   257	    if any(character not in "0123456789abcdef" for character in hex_part):
   258	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError("expected_sha256 must be a lowercase sha256:<64 hex> digest")
   259	    return hex_part
   260	
   261	
   262	def _source_payload(source: str | bytes) -> bytes:
   263	    if isinstance(source, bytes):
   264	        payload = source
   265	    elif isinstance(source, str):
   266	        payload = source.encode("utf-8")
   267	    else:
   268	        raise TypeError("source must be str or bytes")
   269	    try:
   270	        payload.decode("utf-8")
   271	    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
   272	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(
   273	            f"DOE OSTI Semantic Thesaurus export is not valid UTF-8 at byte {error.start}"
   274	        ) from error
   275	    return payload
   276	
   277	
   278	def _iri(term: Identifier, label: str) -> str:
   279	    if not isinstance(term, URIRef):
   280	        kind = type(term).__name__
   281	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(f"{label} must be an IRI, got {kind}")
   282	    return _require_absolute_iri(str(term), label)

   504	def _iri_relations(graph: Graph, predicate_iris: tuple[str, ...], *, label: str) -> tuple[DoeOstiIriRelation, ...]:
   505	    relations: list[DoeOstiIriRelation] = []
   506	    for predicate_iri in predicate_iris:
   507	        for subject, object_ in graph.subject_objects(URIRef(predicate_iri)):
   508	            relations.append(
   509	                DoeOstiIriRelation(
   510	                    subject_iri=_iri(subject, f"{label} subject"),
   511	                    predicate_iri=predicate_iri,
   512	                    object_iri=_iri(object_, f"{label} object"),
   513	                )
   514	            )
   515	    return tuple(sorted(relations, key=lambda item: (item.subject_iri, item.predicate_iri, item.object_iri)))
   516	
   517	
   518	def _concepts(graph: Graph) -> tuple[DoeOstiConcept, ...]:
   519	    concepts: list[DoeOstiConcept] = []
   520	    for subject in set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, SKOS.Concept)):
   521	        concept_iri = _iri(subject, "concept")
   522	        schemes = tuple(sorted(_iri(item, "skos:inScheme object") for item in graph.objects(subject, SKOS.inScheme)))
   523	        top_schemes = tuple(
   524	            sorted(_iri(item, "skos:topConceptOf object") for item in graph.objects(subject, SKOS.topConceptOf))
   525	        )
   526	        concepts.append(DoeOstiConcept(concept_iri=concept_iri, scheme_iris=schemes, top_concept_of_iris=top_schemes))
   527	    return tuple(sorted(concepts, key=lambda item: item.concept_iri))
   528	
   529	
   530	def _concept_schemes(graph: Graph) -> tuple[DoeOstiConceptScheme, ...]:
   531	    schemes: list[DoeOstiConceptScheme] = []
   532	    for subject in set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, SKOS.ConceptScheme)):
   533	        scheme_iri = _iri(subject, "concept scheme")
   534	        top_concepts = tuple(
   535	            sorted(_iri(item, "skos:hasTopConcept object") for item in graph.objects(subject, SKOS.hasTopConcept))
   536	        )
   537	        schemes.append(DoeOstiConceptScheme(scheme_iri=scheme_iri, top_concept_iris=top_concepts))
   538	    return tuple(sorted(schemes, key=lambda item: item.scheme_iri))

   541	def parse_doe_osti_thesaurus_rdfxml(
   542	    source: str | bytes,
   543	    *,
   544	    source_url: str,
   545	    expected_sha256: str | None = None,
   546	    expected_byte_length: int | None = None,
   547	    expected_concept_scheme_iri: str | None = DOE_OSTI_CONCEPT_SCHEME_IRI,
   548	) -> DoeOstiThesaurus:
   549	    """Parse one DOE OSTI Semantic Thesaurus RDF/XML payload into deterministic, lossless feature rows.
   550	
   551	    This never turns a concept's own publisher-supplied numeric IRI into a
   552	    minted identifier of any other shape, and it refuses (rather than drops)
   553	    any predicate or ``rdf:type`` object outside the exact allow-list this
   554	    research pass verified against the real 2020-09-30 distribution.
   555	    """
   556	
   557	    _require_absolute_iri(source_url, "source_url")
   558	    payload = _source_payload(source)
   559	    source_sha256 = _DIGEST_PREFIX + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
   560	    if expected_sha256 is not None:
   561	        _expected_hex(expected_sha256)
   562	        if source_sha256 != expected_sha256:
   563	            raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(f"source digest mismatch: expected {expected_sha256}, got {source_sha256}")
   564	    if expected_byte_length is not None:
   565	        if expected_byte_length <= 0:
   566	            raise DoeOstiThesaurusError("expected_byte_length must be positive")
   567	        if len(payload) != expected_byte_length:
   568	            raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(
   569	                f"source byte length mismatch: expected {expected_byte_length}, got {len(payload)}"
   570	            )
   571	
   572	    graph = Graph()
   573	    try:
   574	        graph.parse(data=payload, publicID=source_url, format="xml")
   575	    except Exception as error:
   576	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(f"could not parse DOE OSTI Semantic Thesaurus RDF/XML: {error}") from error
   577	
   578	    _check_predicate_allow_list(graph)
   579	    _check_rdf_type_allow_list(graph)
   580	
   581	    concept_schemes = _concept_schemes(graph)
   582	    if len(concept_schemes) != 1:
   583	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(f"source must declare exactly one skos:ConceptScheme, found {len(concept_schemes)}")
   584	    concept_scheme_iri = concept_schemes[0].scheme_iri
   585	    if expected_concept_scheme_iri is not None and concept_scheme_iri != expected_concept_scheme_iri:
   586	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(
   587	            f"concept scheme mismatch: expected {expected_concept_scheme_iri!r}, got {concept_scheme_iri!r}"
   588	        )
   589	
   590	    source_iris = tuple(
   591	        sorted(
   592	            {
   593	                _require_absolute_iri(str(term), "source RDF IRI")
   594	                for triple in graph
   595	                for term in triple
   596	                if isinstance(term, URIRef)
   597	            }
   598	        )
   599	    )
   600	    predicate_counts = Counter(str(predicate) for predicate in graph.predicates())
   601	
   602	    return DoeOstiThesaurus(
   603	        source_url=source_url,
   604	        source_sha256=source_sha256,
   605	        source_bytes=len(payload),
   606	        triple_count=len(graph),
   607	        source_iris=source_iris,
   608	        predicate_counts=tuple(
   609	            DoeOstiPredicateCount(predicate_iri=predicate, assertion_count=count)
   610	            for predicate, count in sorted(predicate_counts.items())
   611	        ),
   612	        concept_scheme_iri=concept_scheme_iri,
   613	        concepts=_concepts(graph),
   614	        concept_schemes=concept_schemes,
   615	        labels=_labels(graph),
   616	        notes=_notes(graph),
   617	        semantic_relations=_iri_relations(graph, SEMANTIC_RELATION_PREDICATE_IRIS, label="SKOS semantic relation"),
   618	        structure_relations=_iri_relations(graph, STRUCTURE_RELATION_PREDICATE_IRIS, label="SKOS structure relation"),
   619	    )
   620	
   621	
   622	def parse_doe_osti_thesaurus_file(
   623	    path: Path,
   624	    *,
   625	    source_url: str,
   626	    expected_sha256: str | None = None,
   627	    expected_byte_length: int | None = None,
   628	    expected_concept_scheme_iri: str | None = DOE_OSTI_CONCEPT_SCHEME_IRI,
   629	) -> DoeOstiThesaurus:
   630	    """Parse one local RDF/XML file while retaining its external source identity."""
   631	
   632	    source_path = Path(path)
   633	    if source_path.is_symlink() or not source_path.is_file():
   634	        raise DoeOstiThesaurusError(f"DOE OSTI Semantic Thesaurus source is not a regular file: {source_path}")
   635	    return parse_doe_osti_thesaurus_rdfxml(
   636	        source_path.read_bytes(),
   637	        source_url=source_url,
   638	        expected_sha256=expected_sha256,
   639	        expected_byte_length=expected_byte_length,
   640	        expected_concept_scheme_iri=expected_concept_scheme_iri,
   641	    )

   162	    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
   163	        raise GemetParseError(f"GEMET RDF/XML is not valid UTF-8 at byte {error.start}") from error
   164	    return payload

   279	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   280	class GemetVocabulary:
   281	    """Deterministic parsed view of one exact GEMET RDF/XML payload."""
   282	
   283	    source_url: str
   284	    source_sha256: str
   285	    source_bytes: int
   286	    triple_count: int
   287	    source_iris: tuple[str, ...]
   288	    predicate_counts: tuple[GemetPredicateCount, ...]
   289	    concepts: tuple[GemetConcept, ...]
   290	    concept_schemes: tuple[GemetConceptScheme, ...]
   291	    labels: tuple[GemetLabelExpression, ...]
   292	    notes: tuple[GemetNote, ...]
   293	    notations: tuple[GemetNotation, ...]
   294	    semantic_relations: tuple[GemetIriRelation, ...]
   295	    mapping_relations: tuple[GemetIriRelation, ...]
   296	    license_relations: tuple[GemetIriRelation, ...]
   297	    metadata_literals: tuple[GemetMetadataLiteral, ...]
   298	
   299	    @property
   300	    def counts(self) -> GemetImportCounts:
   301	        labels = Counter(item.role for item in self.labels)
   302	        semantics = Counter(item.predicate_iri for item in self.semantic_relations)
   303	        mappings = Counter(item.predicate_iri for item in self.mapping_relations)
   304	        metadata = Counter(item.property_iri for item in self.metadata_literals)
   305	        return GemetImportCounts(
   306	            source_bytes=self.source_bytes,
   307	            triples=self.triple_count,
   308	            source_iris=len(self.source_iris),
   309	            concepts=len(self.concepts),
   310	            concept_schemes=len(self.concept_schemes),
   311	            preferred_labels=labels["preferred"],
   312	            alternate_labels=labels["alternate"],
   313	            hidden_labels=labels["hidden"],
   314	            notes=len(self.notes),
   315	            notations=len(self.notations),
   316	            broader_relations=semantics[BROADER_PREDICATE_IRI],
   317	            narrower_relations=semantics[NARROWER_PREDICATE_IRI],
   318	            related_relations=semantics[RELATED_PREDICATE_IRI],
   319	            exact_match_relations=mappings[EXACT_MATCH_PREDICATE_IRI],
   320	            close_match_relations=mappings[CLOSE_MATCH_PREDICATE_IRI],
   321	            broad_match_relations=mappings[BROAD_MATCH_PREDICATE_IRI],
   322	            narrow_match_relations=mappings[NARROW_MATCH_PREDICATE_IRI],
   323	            related_match_relations=mappings[RELATED_MATCH_PREDICATE_IRI],
   324	            mapping_relations=len(self.mapping_relations),
   325	            license_relations=len(self.license_relations),
   370	            key=lambda item: (
   371	                item.subject_iri,
   372	                item.property_iri,
   373	                item.value.language_tag or "",
   374	                item.value.lexical_form,
   375	                item.value.datatype_iri or "",
   376	            ),
   377	        )
   378	    )

   381	def _notes(graph: Graph, concept_iris: frozenset[URIRef]) -> tuple[GemetNote, ...]:
   382	    notes: list[GemetNote] = []
   383	    for predicate_iri in GEMET_NOTE_PREDICATE_IRIS:
   384	        predicate = URIRef(predicate_iri)
   385	        for subject, value in graph.subject_objects(predicate):
   386	            if subject not in concept_iris:
   387	                continue
   388	            notes.append(
   389	                GemetNote(
   390	                    subject_iri=_iri(subject, "note subject"),
   391	                    property_iri=predicate_iri,
   392	                    value=_literal(value, f"{predicate_iri} value"),
   393	                )
   394	            )
   395	    return tuple(
   396	        sorted(
   397	            notes,
   398	            key=lambda item: (
   399	                item.subject_iri,
   400	                item.property_iri,
   401	                item.value.language_tag or "",
   402	                item.value.lexical_form,
   403	                item.value.datatype_iri or "",
   404	            ),
   405	        )
   406	    )

   134	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   135	class EuroVocVocabulary:
   136	    """A deterministic, source-faithful EuroVoc SKOS release."""
   137	
   138	    source_url: str
   139	    source_sha256: str
   140	    source_bytes: int
   141	    source_format: LiteralType["turtle", "xml"]
   142	    triple_count: int
   143	    source_iris: tuple[str, ...]
   144	    thesaurus_iri: str
   145	    thesaurus_version: str | None
   146	    domains_scheme_iri: str | None
   147	    domains: tuple[EuroVocDomain, ...]
   148	    domain_groups: tuple[EuroVocDomainGroup, ...]
   149	    concept_schemes: tuple[EuroVocConceptScheme, ...]
   150	    concepts: tuple[EuroVocConcept, ...]
   151	    labels: tuple[EuroVocLabelExpression, ...]
   152	    scheme_memberships: tuple[EuroVocIriRelation, ...]
   153	    top_concept_of_relations: tuple[EuroVocIriRelation, ...]
   154	    has_top_concept_relations: tuple[EuroVocIriRelation, ...]
   155	    hierarchy_relations: tuple[EuroVocIriRelation, ...]
   156	    semantic_relations: tuple[EuroVocIriRelation, ...]
   157	    status_assertions: tuple[EuroVocIriRelation, ...]
   158	
   159	
   160	def _require_absolute_iri(value: str, label: str) -> str:
   360	def _concepts(graph: Graph, domain_iris: set[str]) -> tuple[EuroVocConcept, ...]:
   361	    concepts: list[EuroVocConcept] = []
   362	    for subject in set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, SKOS.Concept)):
   363	        concept_iri = _iri(subject, "concept")
   364	        if concept_iri in domain_iris:
   365	            # EuroVoc models domains as skos:Concept resources. Keep them and
   366	            # ordinary thesaurus concepts as disjoint source record kinds.
   367	            continue
   368	        notation = _required_source_identifier(graph, subject, label="concept")
   369	        concepts.append(EuroVocConcept(concept_iri=concept_iri, notation=notation))
   370	    return tuple(sorted(concepts, key=lambda item: item.concept_iri))
   371	
   372	
   373	def _concept_schemes(graph: Graph) -> tuple[EuroVocConceptScheme, ...]:
   374	    schemes: list[EuroVocConceptScheme] = []
   375	    for subject in set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, SKOS.ConceptScheme)):
   376	        scheme_iri = _iri(subject, "concept scheme")
   377	        notation = _identifier_literal(graph, subject, SKOS.notation, predicate_label="skos:notation")
   378	        schemes.append(EuroVocConceptScheme(scheme_iri=scheme_iri, notation=notation))
   379	    return tuple(sorted(schemes, key=lambda item: item.scheme_iri))
   380	
   381	
   382	def _thesaurus_identity(
   383	    graph: Graph,
   384	    *,
   385	    expected_thesaurus_iri: str | None,
   386	    release_version: str | None,
   387	) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
   388	    rich_subjects = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, EUROVOC_SCHEMA.Thesaurus))
   389	    scheme_subjects = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, SKOS.ConceptScheme))
   390	    if expected_thesaurus_iri is not None:
   391	        subject = URIRef(_require_absolute_iri(expected_thesaurus_iri, "expected_thesaurus_iri"))
   392	        if subject not in scheme_subjects:
   393	            raise EuroVocThesaurusError(
   394	                f"expected EuroVoc thesaurus {expected_thesaurus_iri} is not a skos:ConceptScheme"
   395	            )
   396	    elif len(rich_subjects) == 1:
   397	        subject = next(iter(rich_subjects))
   398	    elif URIRef(EUROVOC_CONCEPT_SCHEME_IRI) in scheme_subjects:
   399	        subject = URIRef(EUROVOC_CONCEPT_SCHEME_IRI)
   400	    elif len(scheme_subjects) == 1:
   401	        subject = next(iter(scheme_subjects))
   402	    else:
   403	        raise EuroVocThesaurusError(
   404	            "EuroVoc RDF must identify one main thesaurus concept scheme"
   405	        )
   406	    thesaurus_iri = _iri(subject, "thesaurus")
   407	    versions = list(graph.objects(subject, OWL.versionInfo))
   408	    if len(versions) > 1 or (versions and not isinstance(versions[0], Literal)):
   409	        raise EuroVocThesaurusError(f"{thesaurus_iri} must have at most one owl:versionInfo literal")
   410	    source_version = str(versions[0]) if versions else None
   411	    if release_version is not None and source_version is not None and source_version != release_version:
   412	        raise EuroVocThesaurusError(
   413	            f"EuroVoc version mismatch: release says {release_version!r}, RDF says {source_version!r}"
   414	        )
   415	    return thesaurus_iri, release_version or source_version
   416	
   417	
   418	def _parse_eurovoc_rdf(
   419	    source: str | bytes,
   420	    *,
   421	    source_url: str,
   422	    rdf_format: LiteralType["turtle", "xml"],
   423	    expected_sha256: str | None = None,
   424	    expected_byte_length: int | None = None,
   425	    expected_thesaurus_iri: str | None = None,
   426	    release_version: str | None = None,
   427	) -> EuroVocVocabulary:
   428	    _require_absolute_iri(source_url, "source_url")
   429	    payload = _source_payload(source)
   430	    source_sha256 = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
   431	    if expected_sha256 is not None:
   432	        if _DIGEST.fullmatch(expected_sha256) is None:
   433	            raise EuroVocThesaurusError("expected_sha256 must be a lowercase sha256:<64 hex> digest")
   434	        if source_sha256 != expected_sha256:
   435	            raise EuroVocThesaurusError(f"source digest mismatch: expected {expected_sha256}, got {source_sha256}")
   436	    if expected_byte_length is not None:
   437	        if expected_byte_length <= 0:
   438	            raise EuroVocThesaurusError("expected_byte_length must be positive")
   439	        if len(payload) != expected_byte_length:
   440	            raise EuroVocThesaurusError(f"source byte length mismatch: expected {expected_byte_length}, got {len(payload)}")
   441	
   442	    graph = Graph()
   443	    try:
   444	        graph.parse(data=payload, format=rdf_format, publicID=source_url)
   445	    except Exception as error:
   446	        raise EuroVocThesaurusError(f"could not parse EuroVoc {rdf_format} RDF: {error}") from error
   447	
   448	    source_iris = tuple(
   449	        sorted(
   450	            {
   451	                _require_absolute_iri(str(term), "source RDF IRI")
   452	                for triple in graph
   453	                for term in triple
   454	                if isinstance(term, URIRef)
   455	            }
   456	        )
   457	    )
   458	
   459	    thesaurus_iri, thesaurus_version = _thesaurus_identity(
   460	        graph,
   461	        expected_thesaurus_iri=expected_thesaurus_iri,
   462	        release_version=release_version,
   463	    )
   464	    domains = _domains(graph)
   465	    domains_by_iri = {item.domain_iri: item for item in domains}
   466	    domain_groups = _domain_groups(graph, domains_by_iri)
   467	    concept_schemes = _concept_schemes(graph)
   468	    concepts = _concepts(graph, set(domains_by_iri))
   469	    domains_scheme_iri = _domains_scheme_iri(graph, domains)
   470	    if domains_scheme_iri is None and any(
   471	        item.scheme_iri == EUROVOC_DOMAINS_SCHEME_IRI for item in concept_schemes
   472	    ):
   473	        domains_scheme_iri = EUROVOC_DOMAINS_SCHEME_IRI
   474	
   475	    return EuroVocVocabulary(
   476	        source_url=source_url,
   477	        source_sha256=source_sha256,
   478	        source_bytes=len(payload),
   479	        source_format=rdf_format,
   480	        triple_count=len(graph),
   481	        source_iris=source_iris,
   482	        thesaurus_iri=thesaurus_iri,
   483	        thesaurus_version=thesaurus_version,
   484	        domains_scheme_iri=domains_scheme_iri,
   485	        domains=domains,
   486	        domain_groups=domain_groups,
   487	        concept_schemes=concept_schemes,
   488	        concepts=concepts,
   489	        labels=_label_expressions(graph),
   490	        scheme_memberships=_iri_relations(graph, (SCHEME_MEMBERSHIP_PREDICATE_IRI,), label="skos:inScheme"),
   491	        top_concept_of_relations=_iri_relations(graph, (TOP_CONCEPT_OF_PREDICATE_IRI,), label="skos:topConceptOf"),
   492	        has_top_concept_relations=_iri_relations(graph, (HAS_TOP_CONCEPT_PREDICATE_IRI,), label="skos:hasTopConcept"),
   493	        hierarchy_relations=_iri_relations(graph, HIERARCHY_PREDICATE_IRIS, label="SKOS hierarchy relation"),
   494	        semantic_relations=_iri_relations(
   495	            graph,
   496	            SEMANTIC_RELATION_PREDICATE_IRIS,
   497	            label="SKOS semantic relation",
   498	        ),
   499	        status_assertions=_iri_relations(graph, (STATUS_PREDICATE_IRI,), label="euvoc:status"),
   500	    )
   501

   503	def parse_eurovoc_turtle(
   504	    source: str | bytes,
   505	    *,
   506	    source_url: str,
   507	    expected_sha256: str | None = None,
   508	    expected_byte_length: int | None = None,
   509	    expected_thesaurus_iri: str | None = None,
   510	    release_version: str | None = None,
   511	) -> EuroVocVocabulary:
   512	    """Parse one EuroVoc Turtle payload without imposing an adoption policy."""
   513	
   514	    return _parse_eurovoc_rdf(
   515	        source,
   516	        source_url=source_url,
   517	        rdf_format="turtle",
   518	        expected_sha256=expected_sha256,
   519	        expected_byte_length=expected_byte_length,
   520	        expected_thesaurus_iri=expected_thesaurus_iri,
   521	        release_version=release_version,
   522	    )

   532	    release_version: str | None = None,
   533	) -> EuroVocVocabulary:

   536	    return _parse_eurovoc_rdf(
   537	        source,
   538	        source_url=source_url,
   539	        rdf_format="xml",
   540	        expected_sha256=expected_sha256,
    55	# Verbatim framing from the source-vocabulary-ontology-thesaurus catalog row

    58	    "Pilot Core only after reconciling the exact release and conflicting CC "
    59	    "BY 4.0 versus broader USDA public-domain/CC0 statements. NALT Core has "
    60	    "about 14,000 concepts; NALT Full is mappings-support and is not "

   257	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   258	class NaltVocabulary:
   259	    """Deterministic parsed view of one exact NALT Turtle payload."""
   260	
   261	    source_url: str
   262	    source_sha256: str
   263	    source_bytes: int
   264	    triple_count: int
   265	    source_iris: tuple[str, ...]
   266	    predicate_counts: tuple[NaltPredicateCount, ...]
   267	    concepts: tuple[NaltConcept, ...]
   268	    concept_schemes: tuple[NaltConceptScheme, ...]
   269	    labels: tuple[NaltLabelExpression, ...]
   270	    semantic_relations: tuple[NaltIriRelation, ...]
   271	    mapping_relations: tuple[NaltIriRelation, ...]
   272	    definition_relations: tuple[NaltIriRelation, ...]
   273	    reified_values: tuple[NaltReifiedLiteral, ...]
   274	    reified_sources: tuple[NaltReifiedLiteral, ...]
   275	    metadata_literals: tuple[NaltMetadataLiteral, ...]
   276	
   277	    @property
   278	    def core_scope_concepts(self) -> tuple[NaltConcept, ...]:
   279	        return tuple(item for item in self.concepts if item.in_core_scope)
   280	
   281	    @property
   282	    def counts(self) -> NaltImportCounts:
   283	        labels = Counter(item.role for item in self.labels)
   284	        semantics = Counter(item.predicate_iri for item in self.semantic_relations)
   285	        metadata = Counter(item.property_iri for item in self.metadata_literals)
   560	            raise NaltCoreError("expected_sha256 must be a lowercase sha256:<64 hex> digest")
   561	        if source_sha256 != expected_sha256:
   562	            raise NaltCoreError(f"source digest mismatch: expected {expected_sha256}, got {source_sha256}")
   563	    if expected_byte_length is not None:
   564	        if expected_byte_length <= 0:
   565	            raise NaltCoreError("expected_byte_length must be positive")
   566	        if len(payload) != expected_byte_length:
   567	            raise NaltCoreError(f"source byte length mismatch: expected {expected_byte_length}, got {len(payload)}")
   568	
   569	    graph = Graph()
   570	    try:
   571	        _parse_lossless_turtle(graph, payload, source_url=source_url)
   572	    except Exception as error:
   573	        raise NaltCoreError(f"could not parse NALT Turtle: {error}") from error
   574	
   575	    source_iris = tuple(
   576	        sorted(
   577	            {
   578	                _require_absolute_iri(str(term), "source RDF IRI")
   579	                for triple in graph
   580	                for term in triple
   581	                if isinstance(term, URIRef)
   582	            }
   583	        )
   584	    )
   585	    predicate_counts = Counter(str(predicate) for predicate in graph.predicates())
   586	
   587	    return NaltVocabulary(
   588	        source_url=source_url,
   589	        source_sha256=source_sha256,
   590	        source_bytes=len(payload),
   591	        triple_count=len(graph),
   592	        source_iris=source_iris,
   593	        predicate_counts=tuple(
   594	            NaltPredicateCount(predicate_iri=predicate, assertion_count=count)
   595	            for predicate, count in sorted(predicate_counts.items())
   596	        ),
   597	        concepts=_concepts(graph),
   598	        concept_schemes=_concept_schemes(graph),
   599	        labels=_labels(graph),
   600	        semantic_relations=_iri_relations(graph, HIERARCHY_PREDICATE_IRIS, label="SKOS hierarchy relation"),
   601	        mapping_relations=_iri_relations(graph, SKOS_MAPPING_PREDICATE_IRIS, label="SKOS mapping relation"),
   602	        definition_relations=_iri_relations(graph, (DEFINITION_PREDICATE_IRI,), label="skos:definition relation"),
   603	        reified_values=_reified_literals(
   604	            graph,
   605	            RDF.value,
   606	            label="reified value",
   607	            require_language_tag=True,
   608	        ),
   609	        reified_sources=_reified_literals(
   610	            graph,
   611	            DCTERMS.source,
   612	            label="reified source",
   613	            require_language_tag=False,
   614	        ),
   615	        metadata_literals=_metadata_literals(graph),
   616	    )

   619	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   620	class NaltCoreCapture:
   140	
   141	def _literal(term: Identifier, label: str) -> NasaThesaurusLiteral:
   142	    if not isinstance(term, Literal):
   143	        raise NasaThesaurusParseError(f"{label} must be an RDF literal")
   144	    language_tag = str(term.language) if term.language is not None else None
   145	    datatype_iri = str(term.datatype) if term.datatype is not None else None
   146	    if datatype_iri is not None:
   147	        _require_absolute_iri(datatype_iri, f"{label} datatype")
   148	    return NasaThesaurusLiteral(
   149	        lexical_form=str(term),
   150	        language_tag=language_tag,
   151	        datatype_iri=datatype_iri,
   152	    )
   153	
   154	
   155	def _source_payload(source: str | bytes) -> bytes:
   156	    if isinstance(source, bytes):
   157	        payload = source
   158	    elif isinstance(source, str):
   159	        payload = source.encode("utf-8")
   160	    else:
   161	        raise TypeError("source must be str or bytes")
   162	    try:
   163	        payload.decode("utf-8")
   164	    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
   165	        raise NasaThesaurusParseError(f"NASA Thesaurus RDF/XML is not valid UTF-8 at byte {error.start}") from error
   166	    return payload

   260	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   261	class NasaThesaurusVocabulary:
   262	    """Deterministic parsed view of one exact NASA Thesaurus RDF/XML payload."""
   263	
   264	    source_url: str
   265	    source_sha256: str
   266	    source_bytes: int
   267	    triple_count: int
   268	    source_iris: tuple[str, ...]
   269	    predicate_counts: tuple[NasaThesaurusPredicateCount, ...]
   270	    concepts: tuple[NasaThesaurusConcept, ...]
   271	    labels: tuple[NasaThesaurusLabelExpression, ...]
   272	    notes: tuple[NasaThesaurusNote, ...]
   273	    semantic_relations: tuple[NasaThesaurusIriRelation, ...]
   274	    use_reference_relations: tuple[NasaThesaurusIriRelation, ...]
   275	    metadata_literals: tuple[NasaThesaurusMetadataLiteral, ...]
   276	    annotation_literals: tuple[NasaThesaurusAnnotationLiteral, ...]
   277	
   278	    @property
   279	    def counts(self) -> NasaThesaurusImportCounts:
   280	        labels = Counter(item.role for item in self.labels)
   281	        semantics = Counter(item.predicate_iri for item in self.semantic_relations)
   282	        use_references = Counter(item.predicate_iri for item in self.use_reference_relations)
   283	        metadata = Counter(item.property_iri for item in self.metadata_literals)
   284	        annotations = Counter(item.property_iri for item in self.annotation_literals)
   285	        return NasaThesaurusImportCounts(
   286	            source_bytes=self.source_bytes,
   287	            triples=self.triple_count,
   288	            source_iris=len(self.source_iris),
   289	            concepts=len(self.concepts),
   290	            preferred_labels=labels["preferred"],
   291	            alternate_labels=labels["alternate"],
   292	            notes=len(self.notes),
   293	            broader_relations=semantics[SKOS_BROADER_PREDICATE_IRI],
   294	            narrower_relations=semantics[SKOS_NARROWER_PREDICATE_IRI],
   295	            related_relations=semantics[SKOS_RELATED_PREDICATE_IRI],
   296	            used_for_relations=use_references[USED_FOR_PREDICATE_IRI],
   297	            use_relations=use_references[USE_INSTEAD_PREDICATE_IRI],
   298	            term_id_assertions=metadata[TERM_ID_PREDICATE_IRI],
   299	            term_vocabulary_assertions=metadata[TERM_VOCABULARY_PREDICATE_IRI],
   300	            term_update_assertions=metadata[TERM_UPDATE_PREDICATE_IRI],
   301	            label_annotations=annotations[LABEL_ANNOTATION_PREDICATE_IRI],
   302	            weight_annotations=annotations[WEIGHT_ANNOTATION_PREDICATE_IRI],
   303	        )
   304	
   305	
   306	def _label_expressions(graph: Graph) -> tuple[NasaThesaurusLabelExpression, ...]:
   307	    properties: tuple[tuple[URIRef, NasaThesaurusLabelRole], ...] = (
   308	        (SKOS.prefLabel, "preferred"),
   309	        (SKOS.altLabel, "alternate"),
   310	    )
   340	    for subject in set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, SKOS.Concept)):
   341	        concept_iri = _iri(subject, "concept")
   342	        count = preferred_count.get(concept_iri, 0)
   343	        if count != 1:
   344	            raise NasaThesaurusParseError(
   345	                f"{concept_iri} has {count} skos:prefLabel assertions; exactly one is required"
   346	            )
   347	        concepts.append(NasaThesaurusConcept(concept_iri=concept_iri))
   348	    return tuple(sorted(concepts, key=lambda item: item.concept_iri))
   349	
   350	
   351	def _notes(graph: Graph) -> tuple[NasaThesaurusNote, ...]:
   352	    notes: list[NasaThesaurusNote] = []
   353	    for subject, value in graph.subject_objects(URIRef(TERM_NOTE_PREDICATE_IRI)):
   354	        subject_iri = _iri(subject, "term note subject")
   355	        literal = _literal(value, "term note value")
   356	        if literal.lexical_form not in KNOWN_TERM_NOTE_MARKERS:
   357	            raise NasaThesaurusParseError(
   358	                f"{subject_iri} has an unrecognized zthes:termNote marker {literal.lexical_form!r}; "
   359	                f"expected one of {KNOWN_TERM_NOTE_MARKERS}"
   360	            )
   361	        notes.append(NasaThesaurusNote(subject_iri=subject_iri, property_iri=TERM_NOTE_PREDICATE_IRI, value=literal))
   362	    return tuple(sorted(notes, key=lambda item: (item.subject_iri, item.value.lexical_form)))
   363	
   364	
   365	def _iri_relations(
   366	    graph: Graph,
   367	    predicate_iris: tuple[str, ...],
   368	    *,
   369	    label: str,
   370	) -> tuple[NasaThesaurusIriRelation, ...]:
   450	    except Exception as error:
   451	        raise NasaThesaurusParseError(f"could not parse NASA Thesaurus RDF/XML: {error}") from error
   452	
   453	    source_iris = tuple(
   454	        sorted(
   455	            {
   456	                _require_absolute_iri(str(term), "source RDF IRI")
   457	                for triple in graph
   458	                for term in triple
   459	                if isinstance(term, URIRef)
   460	            }
   461	        )
   462	    )
   463	    predicate_counts = Counter(str(predicate) for predicate in graph.predicates())
   464	
   465	    labels = _label_expressions(graph)
   466	    return NasaThesaurusVocabulary(
   467	        source_url=source_url,
   468	        source_sha256=source_sha256,
   469	        source_bytes=len(payload),
   470	        triple_count=len(graph),
   471	        source_iris=source_iris,
   472	        predicate_counts=tuple(
   473	            NasaThesaurusPredicateCount(predicate_iri=predicate, assertion_count=count)
   474	            for predicate, count in sorted(predicate_counts.items())
   475	        ),
   476	        concepts=_concepts(graph, labels),
   477	        labels=labels,
   478	        notes=_notes(graph),

   411	def _normalize_doe(parsed: DoeOstiThesaurus, source: RegistryInputPin) -> RegistryRelease:
   412	    member_iris = {concept.concept_iri for concept in parsed.concepts}
   413	    labels: dict[str, list[RegistryLabel]] = defaultdict(list)
   414	    dropped = 0
   415	    for row in parsed.labels:
   416	        if row.subject_iri not in member_iris:
   417	            continue
   418	        if not _english(row.value.language_tag):
   419	            dropped += 1
   420	            continue
   421	        labels[row.subject_iri].append(
   422	            RegistryLabel(
   423	                value=row.value.lexical_form,
   424	                role="preferred",
   425	                source_path=f"{row.subject_iri}::{row.value.language_tag}:skos:prefLabel",
   426	            )
   427	        )
   428	    notes: dict[str, list[Any]] = defaultdict(list)
   429	    for row in parsed.notes:
   430	        if row.subject_iri in member_iris and _english(row.value.language_tag):
   431	            notes[row.subject_iri].append(row)
   432	
   433	    resources: list[RegistryResource] = []
   434	    for concept in parsed.concepts:
   435	        concept_notes = notes.get(concept.concept_iri, ())
   436	        definitions = [row.value.lexical_form for row in concept_notes if row.property_iri == DOE_DEFINITION]
   437	        other_notes = [row.value.lexical_form for row in concept_notes if row.property_iri == DOE_SCOPE_NOTE]
   438	        resources.append(
   439	            RegistryResource(
   440	                iri=concept.concept_iri,
   441	                labels=_sorted_labels(labels[concept.concept_iri]),
   442	                native_payload={
   443	                    "publisherConceptIri": concept.concept_iri,
   444	                    "schemeIris": list(concept.scheme_iris),
   445	                    "topConceptOfIris": list(concept.top_concept_of_iris),
   446	                },
   447	                source_locator=concept.concept_iri,
   448	                source_digest=source.sha256,
   449	                definition=definitions[0] if definitions else None,
   450	                notes=tuple(other_notes + definitions[1:]),
   451	            )
   452	        )
   453	    relations = _direct_relations(parsed.semantic_relations, member_iris)
   454	    return _release(
   455	        key="doe-osti-semantic-thesaurus-2020",
   456	        resource_id="doe-osti-semantic-thesaurus-2020",
   457	        source_module="refspec.registry.doe_osti_thesaurus",
   458	        scope="publisherRelease",
   459	        issued=DOE_OSTI_THESAURUS_V1_2020.stated_publication_date,
   460	        source_release_iri="urn:ref:source-release:doe-osti-thesaurus:v1-2020",
   461	        atlas_release_iri="urn:ref:atlas-release:3:doe-osti-thesaurus:v1-2020",
   462	        scheme_iri="urn:ref:atlas-resource-scheme:doe-osti-semantic-thesaurus-2020",
   463	        source=source,
   464	        resources=resources,
   465	        relations=relations,
   466	        dropped_label_count=dropped,
   467	    )
