   963	   `parquet_search_view.py` all build from the distribution's own compact
   964	   packs — so v1's property restates as: the compact record identity of each
   965	   role must equal the asserted graph's identity for that role. Nothing was
   966	   checking that. The existing check compared per-role counts and five sampled
   967	   rows per pack, and `recordIds` was computed only to feed a digest, so an
   968	   omitted record, an invented one, and a record duplicated across two packs
   969	   all passed. That is now the `explorer-reachability` gate with a negative
   970	   case.
   971	
   972	   The reviewed corpus does not survive contact with the v3 substrate, and the
   973	   measurement is the reason: built against a real compact→Parquet→DuckDB FTS
   974	   view over in-repo CRS evidence, five of seven reviewed entity queries land
   975	   at rank 1, but the one-edit-typo case returns **zero rows** (DuckDB FTS has
   976	   no fuzzy matching) and the prefix case ranks 12th against a reviewed maximum
   977	   of 5 (whole-token matching only). Passing those would mean restating the
   978	   expectations — a check that passes by construction — or adding fuzzy and
   979	   prefix retrieval to the Atlas binding to fit a retired ranker's taxonomy,
   980	   inside the layer SpicySearch owns per REF-022. Two further discoveries make
   981	   the corpus weaker evidence than its name suggests: `maximumRank` carries no
   982	   human judgment (v1 *computed* it from the category and refused any other
   983	   value), and its entity-ring alias cases describe v1 explorer behaviour
   984	   rather than data — v1 synthesised alias forms by splitting a parenthetical
   985	   at render time, and the reviewed concept carries exactly one label. The
   986	   decision is kept falsifiable instead of asserted:
   987	   `test_search_view_matches_whole_tokens_only` fails the day prefix or fuzzy
   988	   retrieval reaches the search view, at which point the corpus becomes
   989	   portable again. Three of its six release identifiers re-derive exactly
   990	   against in-repo bytes; three do not, and ICPSR names a different acquisition
   991	   entirely, so no expectation was invented to cover the gap.
   992	
   993	   Three v1 clauses were examined and deliberately not rebuilt: endpoint and
   994	   filter reachability are not independently violable (the RDF-side release
   995	   checks already force them, so no negative fixture can exist), and facet
   996	   non-vacuity would have been wrong, since a release with zero resources is
   997	   legitimate when it carries only mapping endpoints.
   998	
   999	6. **Deliberately not adopted** until a running check or second consumer
  1000	   demands them: workspaces, warrants (unless P0 closure needs a node
  1125	the only junction between RefSpec and DocSpec, and already assigns topic tagging
  1126	to SpicySearch; that assignment is one row of the wider boundary stated here,
  1127	not reopened by it. REF-022 remains the entry governing the agentic graph search
  1128	direction and its stage gates.
  1129	
  1130	Other decisions and plans link to this entry instead of restating it. The
  1131	duplication is the defect being removed: two independent statements of this
  1132	boundary already existed and had diverged over whether declared version bounds
  1133	suffice to prove a consumable surface. One decision, cited by identifier rather
  1134	than by checkout path, is the fix. This entry changes the day a product's
  1135	published release shape changes; another document needing one of its rows is not
  1136	that day.
  1137	
  1138	### REF-025: Retain canonical Label.id in the next search view
  1139	
  1140	- **Date:** 2026-08-11
  1141	- **Status:** Accepted for the next RefSpec search-view version
  1142	
  1143	The next search-view version retains the canonical `Label.id`. SpicySearch uses
  1144	that identifier directly. No consumer-generated substitute identifier is
  1145	allowed.
  1146	
  1147	A substitute minted downstream is a second label identity with no producer, so
  1148	two products can disagree about which label a row names while each passes its
  1149	own checks. Carrying `Label.id` on the wire removes the disagreement at its
  1150	source rather than reconciling it afterward. This entry changes the day the
  1151	search view stops carrying a canonical label identity; a consumer finding that
  1152	identifier inconvenient is not that day.
  1153	
  1154	### REF-026: Build, prove once, sign, serve — the validation cost reset
  1155	
  1156	- **Date:** 2026-08-12
  1157	- **Status:** Accepted; carried by
  1158	  [plans/validation-cost-reset-plan.md](../plans/validation-cost-reset-plan.md)
  1159	  (v3.5), which holds the measurements, review verdicts, and kill-list this
  1160	  entry ratifies rather than restates.
  1161	
  1162	**The system is four verbs.** Build a vocabulary distribution; prove semantic
  1163	conformance once, at build; sign the result; serve it (Parquet → SpicySearch).
  1164	Structure not serving one of those verbs is guilty until a running consumer is
  1165	named. The prior regime re-derived everything everywhere: measured on the
  1166	32M-quad distribution, independent validation cost ~2h on one core (78% SHACL,
  1167	21% rdflib parse, transport integrity 0.25s), a red build spent 94 minutes
  1168	phrasing a report the fast path had already detected, and reader-side
  1169	re-verification had already drifted (11 gates in the explorer against the
  1170	validator's 13) — independent re-implementation reduces assurance over time.
  1270	**Incremental/exact-reuse subsystem deleted** (`74aaafd9`, −3,485; see
  1271	the REF-019/REF-020 supersessions). With it landed the corpus-wide
  1272	cross-mode SHACL parity sweep (46 cases, release-tier), closing the
  1273	engine-parity gap the plan's findings register named.
  1274	
  1275	Net for the campaign: roughly −147,000 committed lines including the
  1276	corpus, ~−13,700 in production and test code. Carry-forwards, recorded:
  1277	`ManagedReleaseAuthorizationError` is now a public exception raised by
  1278	nothing; `IncrementalPackMaterialization` keeps its wire-tied name until
  1279	the 3.1 bump; the release workflow's acceptance job needs
  1280	`REFSPEC_RELEASE_TIER=1` and a pytest invocation for the parity sweep.
  1281	
  1282	### REF-028: The 3.1 atomic replacement — the wire the campaign could not prove
  1283	
  1284	- **Date:** 2026-08-12
  1285	- **Status:** Accepted; executed (`8ba8d8ea` stage A, `cb10a8e8` stage B).
  1286	  Scoping in [the plan](../plans/validation-cost-reset-plan.md) v3.6 item
  1287	  (4); the three unanimous fable+opus calls in v3.7. Continues REF-027;
  1288	  supersedes REF-015.
  1289	
  1290	**3.1 replaces 3.0 atomically, in place.** Precedent `5c6d889a` — git
  1291	history is the archive. No external consumer of the distribution format

  1295	not an 8,340-file diff, and 3.1 was staged on the bounded Federal Register
  1296	Thesaurus artifact before anything larger. The re-ordering that decision
  1297	recorded held: wire cuts → fresh 3.1 build → *that* is the first sealed
  1298	artifact. Sealing a 3.0 build first would have minted the retiring

/Users/mikewolfd/Work/spicysearch/docs/idea-audit.md:243:**What it is.** Five concrete benchmark-design disciplines: (a) measure first-stage candidate Recall@10/25/50/100/200 *before* ranking, since "your judge cannot recover what the shortlist omits"; (b) sweep rerank depth at 25/50/100/200 rather than fixing one depth, holding candidate sets constant; (c) stratify metrics by query relation — topical relevance, exact citation, authority, amendment/repeal, contrary authority, date/version, cross-document relationship — with the rule that "relation-specific failures remain visible even when excluding them would improve the aggregate" (the ArguAna lesson: finding a counterargument is not the topical-relevance task); (d) an acceptance rule for any ranking change (improve paired nDCG@10 or MRR without reducing Recall@50 by >1 point overall or >3 points in any document profile, preserve all evidence coordinates, meet a predeclared latency/cost envelope); (e) test retrieval-only representations (raw segment / +title / +title+heading path / +title+heading path+source type) where every variant resolves to the same source field, offsets, and text digest — "context is a derived retrieval aid, not evidence."

/Users/mikewolfd/Work/spicysearch/docs/idea-audit.md:470:### Dense-channel field notes: the embedding recipe, the ANN traps, and the diversity quota
/Users/mikewolfd/Work/spicysearch/docs/idea-audit.md:474:Three independent experiments converge on how a dense channel should be built and judged, and all three findings survived the contamination audit as locally computed. (a) **The embedding-input recipe**: use preferred and alternate label keywords, immediate parent keywords, immediate child keywords, and definition or scope-note keywords when present; do *not* add scheme names, provenance prose, or serialized RDF; compare the signal scores separately so a reviewer can see whether a pair matched by label, hierarchy, definition, or several. This is the designed answer to the measured boilerplate problem — 8 templates cover 100% of concepts and 74% of the median embedding string, and removing them raises query top-1 cosine 0.6042 → 0.6512 like-for-like. (b) **The ANN traps**: memory and recall proved to be one dial (the only configuration matching the exact oracle everywhere saves 4.7% memory; cheaper settings lose 21–74% of the exact top-12), and the structural cause is that the exact top-50 sits inside a **0.056-wide cosine band**, giving HNSW's greedy descent almost no gradient — so any graph ANN struggles on these vectors, not just usearch. Two named misreadings: a configuration holding 4/8 at 26% recall reads as "ANN is harmless" but actually proves the dense channel is not carrying those targets, and `f16-c32` beats `f16` on aggregate recall while scoring 0/8 versus 2/8 on the oracle. Rule: **judge a candidate channel by the oracle, never by recall alone.** (c) **The diversity quota**: adding dense retrieval to the lexical pair leaves the oracle unchanged (4/8) while mean rank drops 5.25 → 2.0 — the dense channel *reorders* what lexical already found rather than finding more — and dropping the source-vocabulary quota reaches 5/8 while adequate-kept collapses 4/5 → 2/5 as one scheme floods 75% of slots.

SpicySearch runs multiple named channels (`src/spicysearch/engine.py:298-418`) with no fusion policy and no diversity constraint, and its semantic slot is designed-but-dark.

/Users/mikewolfd/Work/spicysearch/docs/idea-audit.md:738:**Why it matters:** the deletion-propagation rule is the one that gets structurally harder every day this platform runs. The architecture now converges on immutable, digest-pinned, content-addressed releases plus disposable indexes and embeddings; "how does a redaction request reach an already-published immutable release?" has no answer in the current design and no place where the question is even recorded. Comments are also the single richest source in the corpus, so "participation records do not enter the general pipeline by default" is a decision someone will make implicitly the first time a comment corpus is ingested.

/Users/mikewolfd/Work/spicysearch/docs/idea-audit.md:470:### Dense-channel field notes: the embedding recipe, the ANN traps, and the diversity quota
/Users/mikewolfd/Work/spicysearch/docs/idea-audit.md:474:Three independent experiments converge on how a dense channel should be built and judged, and all three findings survived the contamination audit as locally computed. (a) **The embedding-input recipe**: use preferred and alternate label keywords, immediate parent keywords, immediate child keywords, and definition or scope-note keywords when present; do *not* add scheme names, provenance prose, or serialized RDF; compare the signal scores separately so a reviewer can see whether a pair matched by label, hierarchy, definition, or several. This is the designed answer to the measured boilerplate problem — 8 templates cover 100% of concepts and 74% of the median embedding string, and removing them raises query top-1 cosine 0.6042 → 0.6512 like-for-like. (b) **The ANN traps**: memory and recall proved to be one dial (the only configuration matching the exact oracle everywhere saves 4.7% memory; cheaper settings lose 21–74% of the exact top-12), and the structural cause is that the exact top-50 sits inside a **0.056-wide cosine band**, giving HNSW's greedy descent almost no gradient — so any graph ANN struggles on these vectors, not just usearch. Two named misreadings: a configuration holding 4/8 at 26% recall reads as "ANN is harmless" but actually proves the dense channel is not carrying those targets, and `f16-c32` beats `f16` on aggregate recall while scoring 0/8 versus 2/8 on the oracle. Rule: **judge a candidate channel by the oracle, never by recall alone.** (c) **The diversity quota**: adding dense retrieval to the lexical pair leaves the oracle unchanged (4/8) while mean rank drops 5.25 → 2.0 — the dense channel *reorders* what lexical already found rather than finding more — and dropping the source-vocabulary quota reaches 5/8 while adequate-kept collapses 4/5 → 2/5 as one scheme floods 75% of slots.
/Users/mikewolfd/Work/spicysearch/docs/idea-audit.md:476:**Current status — the usearch rejection is decided and recorded with a revisit trigger; the transferable field notes are not carried to the new owner.** Grepping `scope note|embedding text|parent keyword|boilerplate|embedding input` and `rrf|reciprocal rank|quota|diversity|round.robin|interleav` across spicysearch's `src/`, `docs/` and `evaluation/` returns zero hits.    645	                "topDocumentIds": top_documents[query.variant_id],
   646	                "variantId": query.variant_id,
   647	            }
   648	        )
   649	    means = {
   650	        name: sum(cases[query.variant_id]["metrics"][name] for query in queries) / len(queries)
   651	        for name in RANKED_METRICS
   652	    }
   653	    return {
   654	        "armId": arm_id,
   655	        "conceptGateOpenCount": sum(1 for gate in gates.values() if gate["gateOpened"]),
   656	        "conceptLaneContributionCount": sum(gate["conceptContributionCount"] for gate in gates.values()),
   657	        "lanes": list(ARM_LANES[arm_id]),
   658	        "metrics": {name: _fixed(means[name]) for name in RANKED_METRICS},
   659	        "queries": per_query,
   660	        "retrievalMode": ARM_MODES[arm_id],
   661	        "scoreStatus": score["status"],
   662	        "scoredQueryCount": score["scored"],
   663	        "_raw_means": means,
   664	    }
   665	
   666	
   667	def _lane_reach(runtime: Any, lookup: VocabularyLookup) -> dict[str, Any]:
   668	    """Probe how far the concept lane can reach, in counts and never in scores.
   669	
   670	    This probe runs each vocabulary label as its own query and reports what the
   671	    lane then does. There is no fixed relevance set for a bare label, so nothing
   672	    here is scored and nothing here is a quality claim: it separates a lane that
   673	    never runs from a lane that runs and changes nothing. It was the only way to
   674	    see the lane at all while the gate required the complete normalized query to
   675	    equal a complete normalized label; under in-query span resolution it stays
   676	    as the isolated per-label reading of the same lane.
   677	    """
   678	
   679	    labels = sorted({label.raw_label for label in lookup.labels})
   680	    probes = []
   681	    for raw_label in labels:
   682	        responses = {
   683	            arm_id: runtime.search(
   684	                SearchRequest(
   685	                    raw_query=raw_label,
   686	                    plan=parse_query(raw_label),
   687	                    limit=RESULT_LIMIT,
   688	                    page=RESULT_PAGE,
   689	                    mode=ARM_MODES[arm_id],
   690	                )
   691	            )
   692	            for arm_id in ARM_IDS
   693	        }
   694	        treatment = responses[TREATMENT_ARM]
   695	        baseline = responses[BASELINE_ARM]
   696	        gate = _concept_gate(treatment)
   697	        baseline_ranks = {result.document_id: rank for rank, result in enumerate(baseline.results, start=1)}
   698	        treatment_ranks = {result.document_id: rank for rank, result in enumerate(treatment.results, start=1)}
   699	        added = sorted(set(treatment_ranks) - set(baseline_ranks))
   700	        moved = sorted(
   701	            document_id
   702	            for document_id, rank in treatment_ranks.items()
   703	            if document_id in baseline_ranks and baseline_ranks[document_id] != rank
   704	        )
   705	        probes.append(
   706	            {
   707	                "addedDocumentIds": added,
   708	                "conceptContributionCount": gate["conceptContributionCount"],
   709	                "gateOpened": gate["gateOpened"],
   710	                "label": raw_label,
   711	                "rerankedDocumentIds": moved,
   712	                "resolvedConceptIds": gate["resolvedConceptIds"],
   713	            }
   714	        )
   715	    return {
   716	        "basis": "one query per distinct vocabulary label; unscored, counts only",
   717	        "gateOpenLabelCount": sum(1 for probe in probes if probe["gateOpened"]),
   718	        "labelCount": len(labels),
   719	        "labelsAddingDocuments": sum(1 for probe in probes if probe["addedDocumentIds"]),
   720	        "labelsRerankingDocuments": sum(1 for probe in probes if probe["rerankedDocumentIds"]),
   721	        "probes": probes,
   722	    }

   724	
   725	def _movers(baseline: Mapping[str, Any], treatment: Mapping[str, Any], metric: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
     1	# SpicySearch MVP plan
     2	
     3	Last reconciled on 2026-08-12 after the product owner settled document
     4	processing, label identity, topic-tagging ownership, and the concept lane's
     5	query-side gate. Current code and
     6	accepted decisions define the target. Historical formats, measurements, and
     7	retired implementations do not. Reuse code only when it is the shortest path
     8	to this target; add no compatibility work merely to preserve it.
     9	
    10	## MVP outcome
    11	
    12	A user can search every selected document in one sealed corpus through the CLI
    13	and HTTP API. Search ranks source-grounded `searchSegment` records, returns
    14	document results with the best matching segments, preserves exact evidence,
    15	and explains the corpus and snapshot searched.
    16	
    17	The same search surface retains two additional evidence-bearing candidate
    18	lanes. Semantic retrieval finds differently worded `searchSegment` records
    19	through one pinned embedding provider. Concept retrieval resolves a query
    20	against one small RefSpec Atlas release and retrieves snapshot-scoped topic
    21	tags built inside SpicySearch from DocSpec segments. Neither lane creates source
    22	facts or legal conclusions, and neither changes tags at request time.
    23	
    24	For the MVP, **all documents** means every member selected for search by one
    25	named, immutable `SourceCatalogRelease`. Let `U` be the complete requested
    26	universe, `S` the selected subset fixed before capture, and `N` the cardinality
    27	of `S`. The release records both set digests and partitions every member of
    28	`U`. A later capture or processing failure blocks completion; it cannot shrink
    29	`S` or `N`.
    30	
    31	## Locked product boundaries
    32	
    33	REF-024 in `../spicy-regs/RefSpec/docs/decisions.md` is the canonical statement
    34	of who owns what across the five products. It governs; the table below is a
    35	working summary for this plan.
    36	
    37	| Product | Owns | Does not own |
    38	| --- | --- | --- |
    39	| Rulespec Core | Portable source-catalog and document-release schemas, canonical identity rules, validators, generated types, diagnostic codes, and conformance fixtures | Source data, vocabulary content, document processing, or search |
    40	| SpicyRegs | Regulatory source discovery, source identity, source-issued versions, exact source-native metadata, source observations, candidate renditions, selection, discovery coverage, and selection coverage | Capture, content extraction, segmentation, `DocumentRelease`, or search indexes |
    41	| DocSpec | Rendition capture, capture coverage, exact retained bytes, human-readable representations, structural nodes, bounded search segments, evidence coordinates, processing coverage, release membership, and the published `DocumentRelease` | Regulatory meaning, vocabulary authority, ranking, or serving |
    42	| RefSpec | Vocabulary sources, concepts, preferred and alternate labels, relations, source evidence, release policy, and sealed Atlas distributions | Document processing, document-to-concept claims, document ranking, or search serving |
    43	| Rulespec Extrapolator | Rulespec-based logical structuring and evidence-linked rule extraction from prepared DocSpec segments | Document capture, vocabulary publication, search topic tagging, ranking, or serving |
    44	| SpicySearch | Release admission, snapshot-scoped document-to-topic tagging, backend-neutral search ports, backend composition, `SearchSnapshot`, disposable indexes, query processing, filters, deterministic ranking, results, explanations, coverage, CLI, and HTTP serving | Source or corpus authority, vocabulary publication, canonical topic assignments, or legal conclusions |
    45	
    46	Publishing an artifact does not transfer upstream authority. DocSpec carries
    47	SpicyRegs facts and identifiers without reinterpreting them. SpicySearch topic
    48	tags are disposable retrieval signals, not RefSpec facts, Rulespec assignments,
    49	or source claims.
    50	
    51	## Artifact flow
    52	
    53	```text
    54	Rulespec Core schema set
    55	        |
    56	        +--> SpicyRegs SourceCatalogRelease
    57	        |              |
    58	        |              v
    59	        +---------> DocSpec DocumentRelease -------------------+
    60	                                                              |
    61	RefSpec single-scheme Atlas release --> Parquet search view ---+--> SpicySearch SearchSnapshot
    62	                                                                     |
    63	                                                                     +--> CLI
    64	                                                                     +--> POST /v1/search
    65	```
    66	
    67	There is no DocSpec-to-RefSpec edge and no search-time join between independent
    68	document releases. Every MVP snapshot consumes exactly one DocSpec
    69	`DocumentRelease` and one RefSpec `AtlasParquetSearchViewManifest`. RefSpec
    70	verifies the search view against the single-scheme Atlas release before
    71	publication. During snapshot build, SpicySearch creates a closed set of topic
    72	tags against those exact inputs and rejects any tag whose document, segment,
    73	concept, release, or evidence does not resolve exactly. Tags may change between
    74	snapshots; a published snapshot never changes them.
    75	
    76	Every cross-product input must be a complete, immutable, digest-pinned
    77	distribution with relative member paths. One root distribution digest is the
    78	cross-product pin; its closed manifest carries the member digests. Consumers
    79	recompute the root and member digests at admission and open, and reject missing,
    80	extra, escaped, symlinked-outside, duplicate, unknown-schema, or mismatched
    81	members. Expensive semantic recomputation runs once at the producer's build
    82	gate before publication. Producers publish by atomic rename or an equivalent
    83	conditional create. Do not add repeated ambient receipts or worktree file
    84	hashes around the same handoff.
    85	
    86	REF-026 in `../spicy-regs/RefSpec/docs/decisions.md` governs RefSpec's sealed
    87	publication: `verify_seal` covers signature, structural read, manifest and
    88	acceptance-receipt digests, symlink and type sweep, and a pinned closed-
    89	membership walk of every member — so admitting a sealed RefSpec artifact
    90	through `verify_seal` satisfies this section's admission rules for that
    91	input. Admission adopts `refspec-distribution-seal-2` (REF-028): the payload
    92	binds `manifestSha256`, `acceptanceSha256`, and `parquetViewManifestSha256`,
    93	so the served Parquet view is seal-covered and the compact JSONL wire is
    94	gone. RefSpec's first seal mints over its 3.1 distribution format, and a
    95	search-view 1.2 is expected (five undeclared warrant-field omissions in 1.1's
    96	evidence-binding rows get declared or carried); the admission pin here moves
    97	when that view publishes.
    98	
    99	## Code and data boundaries
   100	
   101	Reusable code crosses repositories only as a published, versioned package with
   102	declared version bounds plus a hard-failing installed-wheel conformance test. A
   103	valid version number alone does not prove that the required symbols still exist.
   104	There is no universal public-symbol manifest: a manifest is a second declaration
   105	of the surface and drifts; a consumer test does not. Rulespec's
   106	`make test-package` is the working instance. Add a manifest only where a
   107	package cannot express its required surface through a focused consumer test.
   108	
   109	Cross-product data crosses only as a digest-named release. The MVP may share the
   110	Rulespec Core package for schemas, generated types, identity functions, and
   111	structural validation. The Rulespec schemas arrive as one digest-addressed
   112	bundle inside the Rulespec Core wheel; there is no second schema-publication
   113	pipeline. That wheel must include the new source and document schemas, generated
   114	types, identity helpers, diagnostics, and valid and invalid fixtures. SpicyRegs,
   115	DocSpec, RefSpec, and SpicySearch do not import one another's business logic.
   116	
   117	No build or runtime reads another product's checkout, editable install, mutable
   118	database, or developer cache. Each product package contains only code used by
   119	its build, publication, validation, or serving path; research tools remain
   120	repository-local.
   121	
   122	## Retrieval-lane dependency injection
   123	
   124	Treat every retrieval implementation as a replaceable adapter. SpicySearch
   125	uses explicit constructor injection through small Python `Protocol` interfaces;
   126	it does not need a dependency-injection framework. Backend-neutral search code
   127	never imports or constructs a concrete lexical engine, embedding model, vector
   128	index, concept postings engine, or model client. SpicySearch may use DuckDB
   129	separately for owned catalog and join work, but the core never opens or
   130	interprets provider members.
   131	
   132	```text
   133	explicit build configuration -----+
   134	                                   +--> allowlisted composition root --> lexical provider
   135	sealed lane selections at open ----+                                --> semantic provider
   136	                                                                    --> concept provider
   137	                                                                          |--> builders
   138	                                                                          |--> verifiers
   139	                                                                          +--> sessions --> search core --> CLI / HTTP
   140	```
   141	
   142	Each lane uses the same four backend-neutral roles:
   143	
   144	- a provider exposes an immutable lane descriptor and capabilities and creates
   145	  builders, verifiers, and query sessions;
   146	- a builder consumes canonical lane records and returns an opaque, closed set
   147	  of relative members plus a build receipt;
   148	- a verifier checks provider-specific behavior at the producer gate and
   149	  compatibility at open; and
   150	- a session is a long-lived, closeable reader that accepts a canonical lane
   151	  query and returns canonical candidate hits.
   152	
   153	`SearchBackendProvider` remains the lexical specialization. Semantic providers
   154	consume DocSpec segments and own windowing, embedding calls, vector bytes,
   155	model receipts, and similarity execution. SpicySearch keeps topic generation
   156	behind one small internal build interface so the implementation can change or
   157	move later without creating a service now. Concept providers consume verified
   158	snapshot-local topic tags and own concept-postings bytes and lookup execution;
   159	query-label resolution, allowed relation traversal, tag evidence hydration, and
   160	coverage remain core policy.
   161	
   162	An adapter owns engine-specific filenames, media types, schemas, connections,
   163	temporary resources, native queries, model loading, behavior verification, and
   164	cleanup. The core owns request parsing, Unicode normalization, typed filters,
   165	lane activation, the canonical query plans, candidate-set bounds, fixed score
   166	conversion, deterministic fusion, complete document aggregation before
   167	pagination, snippets, evidence, coverage, suggestions, and response formatting.
   168	Backend types, native scores, vectors, connections, and query strings never
   169	cross an adapter boundary.
   170	
   171	Each provider declares a closed descriptor containing its lane kind and
   172	interface version, provider or adapter identity, engine or model identity and
   173	revision, index-format ID, required runtime dependency pins, and one
   174	behavior-bearing configuration digest. That single digest covers analyzer or
   175	embedding policy, query plans, and the capability profile; none of them carries
   176	a separate descriptor digest. Resource settings such as thread count, memory limit,
   177	scratch path, endpoint, or resource pool size stay out of behavior identity
   178	unless they can change results. Credentials never appear in a descriptor,
   179	receipt, log, snapshot, or identity.
   180	
   181	Composition roots inject an isolated scratch location outside the immutable
   182	snapshot. Builders, verifiers, sessions, and provider-owned pools use managed
   183	context-manager lifecycles with idempotent close, clean up after success,
   184	refusal, cancellation, or failure, and declare whether they support concurrent
   185	reads. An engine error becomes a stable SpicySearch backend-failure code; it
   186	never becomes an empty result, a partial result, or a fallback to a different
   187	provider.
   188	
   189	The snapshot-build CLI is a composition root. Its explicit configuration names
   190	one allowlisted provider for each lane and injects all three into build and
   191	verification. Snapshot verify, CLI query, and HTTP startup read the three sealed
   192	selections, resolve only operator-allowed providers, and inject them. They never
   193	import a module path named by a snapshot. Library constructors require their
   194	dependencies; they have no `None` provider, module-global service locator,
   195	mutable registry, automatic model construction, or `backend or
   196	DuckDBFTSBackend()` fallback.
   197	
   198	`SearchBehaviorPolicy` determines user-visible search meaning. Separate sealed
   199	lane selections record all provider descriptors and capabilities. Versioned
   200	capability profiles state what the policy requires: lexical completeness before
   201	document aggregation; a sealed semantic candidate depth, deterministic total
   202	ordering, exact rescore, and model pin; and exact concept-postings completeness,
   203	topic-tag evidence, coverage, and deterministic resolution. Build and open
   204	reject unknown providers, descriptor mismatches, missing capabilities, model
   205	drift, or topic-tagging-policy drift before touching an index. No lane may be
   206	silently disabled, replaced, or treated as an empty result after failure.
   207	
   208	Each snapshot uses exactly one lexical, one semantic, and one concept provider.
   209	Changing any provider, adapter, engine or model version, model revision, index
   210	format, behavior-bearing configuration, or capability requires a new snapshot
   211	and logical identity. A provider may emit one or many physical members;
   212	SpicySearch verifies their closed membership and digests, and that provider
   213	alone interprets them. Network-managed or mutable search services remain
   214	outside this offline MVP until a separate decision defines their publication,
   215	persistence, availability, and verification rules.
   216	
   217	## Execution order
   218	
   219	### 1. Define the portable corpus schemas
   220	
   221	**Owner:** Rulespec Core
   222	
   223	Publish one versioned schema set for:
   224	
   225	- `SourceCatalogRelease` and `DocumentRelease` roots and member manifests;
   226	- source items, source-native metadata, candidate renditions, and source
   227	  dispositions;
   228	- captured files, representations, source-derived `structuralNode` records,
   229	  bounded `searchSegment` records, and reversible evidence coordinates;
   230	- processing dispositions, failures, coverage, and build receipts; and
   231	- canonical identifiers, canonical set digests, distribution digests,
   232	  diagnostic codes, and first-failure order.
   233	
   234	First publish immutable candidate schema and fixture bytes under a digest. That
   235	lets each downstream product implement against the same bytes without waiting
   236	for every other implementation. Provide sealed valid and invalid fixtures that
   237	SpicyRegs, DocSpec, and SpicySearch verify independently. The final Rulespec
   238	release must reuse the tested candidate bytes unchanged; any edit starts a new
   239	candidate. Schema ownership does not grant Rulespec authority over the records
   240	carried by those schemas.
   241	
   242	**Exit gate:** the candidate schema set is immutable and digest-named, its own
   243	validator returns the expected verdict and diagnostic code for every fixture,
   244	and the bytes are available through a versioned Rulespec Core package and a
   245	sealed schema release. Cross-product verdict agreement closes at Step 7.
   246	
   247	### 2. Publish the complete regulatory source catalog
   248	
   249	**Owner:** SpicyRegs
   250	
   251	Publish one sealed `SourceCatalogRelease` containing the complete requested
   252	universe `U` and the selected set `S`. The release root records the selection
   253	policy, `requestedUniverseSetDigest`, and `selectedSourceSetDigest`. Each source
   254	item must include:
   255	
   256	- a stable `sourceItemId`, regulatory `documentId`, and source-issued version;
   257	- exact source-native metadata plus the normalized MVP fields: title, agency,
   258	  document type, publication and update dates, docket identifiers, Regulation
   259	  Identifier Numbers (RINs), comment closing date, language, and source URL;
   260	- source-observed topics and other observations, kept distinct from RefSpec

  1411	    # A declared exclusion names an entity layer by rdf:type or IRI prefix, and
  1412	    # publishers describe those entities with blank nodes too -- void:classPartition
  1413	    # hangs its per-class counts off one. Those claims never reach iri_claims or
  1414	    # literal_claims (both need an IRI subject), so the exclusion has to reach
  1415	    # them here or they would be reported as uncovered while the layer they
  1416	    # belong to is declared. The closure follows blank nodes out of an excluded
  1417	    # subject and no further: a blank node reachable from anything else stays in
  1418	    # the uncovered report.
  1419	    excluded_blank_node_claims: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
  1420	    exclusion_nodes: list[tuple[str, set[Any]]] = []
  1421	    for exclusion in declared_claim_exclusions:
  1422	        roots = {
  1423	            term
  1424	            for term in graph.subjects()
  1425	            if isinstance(term, rdflib.URIRef)
  1426	            and exclusion.selects(
  1427	                str(term),
  1428	                frozenset(
  1429	                    str(value) for value in graph.objects(term, rdflib.RDF.type)
  1430	                ),
  1431	            )
  1432	        }
  1433	        reached: set[Any] = set(roots)
  1434	        frontier = list(roots)
  1435	        while frontier:
  1436	            for obj in graph.objects(frontier.pop(), None):
  1437	                if isinstance(obj, rdflib.BNode) and obj not in reached:
  1438	                    reached.add(obj)
  1439	                    frontier.append(obj)
  1440	        if roots:
  1441	            exclusion_nodes.append((exclusion.name, reached))
  1442	            excluded_blank_node_claims[exclusion.name] = []
  1443	    for subject, predicate, obj in graph:
  1444	        if not isinstance(subject, rdflib.BNode) and not isinstance(obj, rdflib.BNode):
  1445	            continue
  1446	        supported_label_edge = (
  1447	            isinstance(subject, rdflib.URIRef)
  1448	            and str(predicate) in SKOSXL_LABEL_PREDICATES
  1449	            and obj in label_nodes
  1450	        )
  1451	        supported_label_form = (
  1452	            subject in label_nodes
  1453	            and str(predicate) == SKOSXL_LITERAL_FORM
  1454	            and isinstance(obj, rdflib.Literal)
  1455	        )
  1456	        if supported_label_edge or supported_label_form:
  1457	            continue
  1458	        detail = (
  1459	            f"publisher blank-node claim {subject!r} <{predicate}> {obj!r} has no "
  1460	            "executable source-shape inverse"
  1461	        )
  1462	        declaring = next(
  1463	            (name for name, nodes in exclusion_nodes if subject in nodes),
  1464	            None,
  1465	        )
  1466	        if declaring is not None:
  1467	            if detail not in excluded_blank_node_claims[declaring]:
  1468	                excluded_blank_node_claims[declaring].append(detail)
  1469	            continue
  1470	        if detail not in unevaluated_claims:
  1471	            unevaluated_claims.append(detail)
  1472	            defects.append(Finding(kind="source", source=source, detail=detail))
  1473	    resource_predicate_counts: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = defaultdict(int)
  1474	    for subject, predicate, _ in graph:
  1475	        if isinstance(subject, rdflib.URIRef) and str(subject) in resource_iris:
  1476	            resource_predicate_counts[(str(subject), str(predicate))] += 1
  1477	
  1478	    return PublisherView(
  1479	        concepts=frozenset(concepts),
  1480	        schemes=frozenset(schemes),
  1481	        pref_labels={key: frozenset(value) for key, value in pref.items()},
  1482	        alt_labels={key: frozenset(value) for key, value in alt.items()},
  1483	        hidden_labels={key: frozenset(value) for key, value in hidden.items()},
  1484	        notations={key: frozenset(value) for key, value in notations.items()},
  1485	        annotations=frozenset(annotations),
  1486	        resource_annotations=frozenset(resource_annotations),
  1487	        resource_annotation_target_claim_counts={
  1488	            target: sum(1 for _ in graph.predicate_objects(rdflib.URIRef(target)))
  1489	            for target in sorted(resource_annotation_targets)
  1490	        },
  1491	        literal_claims=literal_claims,
  1492	        iri_claims=iri_claims,
  1493	        reified_statements=frozenset(reified_statements),
  1494	        pref_label_count_all_languages=pref_all,
  1495	        alt_label_count_all_languages=alt_all,
  1496	        hidden_label_count_all_languages=hidden_all,
  1497	        relations=frozenset(relations),
  1498	        memberships=memberships,
  1499	        top_concept_of=top_concept_of,
  1500	        has_top_concept=has_top_concept,
  1501	        resource_predicate_counts=dict(resource_predicate_counts),
  1502	        defects=tuple(defects),
  1503	        resource_input_digests=dict(resource_input_digests or {}),
  1504	        input_content_digests=dict(input_content_digests or {}),
  1505	        unevaluated_claims=tuple(dict.fromkeys(unevaluated_claims)),
  1506	        declared_out_of_scope_blank_node_claims={
  1507	            name: tuple(details)
  1508	            for name, details in excluded_blank_node_claims.items()
  1509	        },
  1510	    )
  1511	
  1512	
  1513	def read_publisher_skos(path: Path, fmt: str, source: str, zip_member: str | None = None) -> PublisherView:
  1514	    """Read one pinned SKOS distribution into the comparison form."""
  1515	    return _publisher_view(_load_graph(path, fmt, zip_member), source)

  1517	
  1518	def _resolve_source_pin(source_root: Path, pin: SourcePin) -> Path:
  1519	    """Resolve a declared input without allowing it to escape the two approved roots."""
  1520	    candidates = (source_root / pin.path, REPOSITORY_ROOT / pin.path)
  1521	    for candidate in candidates:
  1522	        if candidate.is_file() and not candidate.is_symlink():
  1523	            return candidate
  1524	    return candidates[0]
  1525	
  1526	
  1527	def _read_publisher_pin_set(
  1528	    inputs: Sequence[SourcePin],
  1529	    source: str,
  1530	    authenticated_payloads: Mapping[SourcePin, bytes],
  1531	    *,
  1532	    additional_annotation_predicates: Sequence[str] = (),
  1533	    additional_relation_predicates: Sequence[str] = (),
  1534	    declared_claim_exclusions: Sequence[DeclaredClaimExclusion] = (),
  1535	) -> PublisherView:
  1536	    """Read all RDF inputs, reporting every unreadable member before failing the set."""
  1537	    import rdflib
  1538	
  1539	    graph = rdflib.Graph()
  1540	    failures: list[str] = []
  1541	    resource_input_digests: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
  1542	    input_content_digests: dict[str, str] = {}
  1543	    for pin in inputs:
  1544	        try:
  1545	            payload = authenticated_payloads[pin]
  1546	            loaded = _load_graph_payload(
  1547	                payload,
  1548	                pin.fmt,
  1549	                pin.zip_member,
  1550	                public_id=pin.source_iri,
  1551	            )
  1552	            content = payload
  1553	            if pin.zip_member is not None:
  1554	                with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(payload)) as archive:
  1555	                    content = archive.read(pin.zip_member)
  1556	        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - inspect the remaining declared inputs
  1557	            failures.append(f"{pin.path}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
  1558	            continue
  1559	        content_digest = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
  1560	        input_content_digests[pin.path] = content_digest
  1561	        for subject in loaded.subjects():
  1562	            if isinstance(subject, rdflib.URIRef):
  1563	                resource_input_digests[str(subject)].add(content_digest)
  1564	        graph += loaded
  1565	        for prefix, namespace in loaded.namespaces():
  1566	            graph.bind(prefix, namespace, replace=True)
  1567	    if failures:
  1568	        raise ValueError("; ".join(failures))
  1569	    return _publisher_view(
  1570	        graph,
  1571	        source,
  1572	        additional_annotation_predicates=additional_annotation_predicates,
  1573	        additional_relation_predicates=additional_relation_predicates,
  1574	        resource_input_digests={
  1575	            resource: frozenset(digests)
  1576	            for resource, digests in resource_input_digests.items()
  1577	        },
  1578	        input_content_digests=input_content_digests,
  1579	        declared_claim_exclusions=declared_claim_exclusions,
  1580	    )
  1581	
  1582	
  1583	def read_publisher_inputs(source_root: Path, spec: SourceSpec) -> PublisherView:
  1584	    """Read and union every independently pinned RDF input for one comparison scope."""
  1585	    payloads = {
  1586	        pin: read_verified_file_pin(
  1587	            _resolve_source_pin(source_root, pin),
  1588	            expected_sha256=pin.sha256,
  1589	            expected_byte_length=pin.byte_length,
  1590	            logical_path=pin.path,
  1591	        )
  1592	        for pin in spec.inputs
  1593	    }
  1594	    view = _select_publisher_view(
  1595	        _read_publisher_pin_set(
  1596	            spec.inputs,
  1597	            spec.name,
  1598	            payloads,
  1599	            additional_annotation_predicates=(
  1600	                spec.rdf_source.additional_annotation_predicates
  1601	                if spec.rdf_source is not None
  1602	                else ()
  1603	            ),
  1604	            additional_relation_predicates=(
  1605	                spec.rdf_source.additional_relation_predicates
  1606	                if spec.rdf_source is not None
  1607	                else ()
  1608	            ),
  1609	            declared_claim_exclusions=spec.declared_claim_exclusions,
  1610	        ),
  1611	        spec.subset,
  1612	    )
  1613	    return _select_publisher_concepts(view, spec.included_concept_iris)

  1616	def _publisher_source_scheme_subjects(view: PublisherView) -> frozenset[str]:
  1617	    """Return explicit and referenced publisher-native scheme IRIs."""
  1618	    return frozenset(
  1619	        {
  1620	            *view.schemes,
  1621	            *(scheme for _, scheme in view.memberships),
  1622	            *(scheme for _, scheme in view.top_concept_of),
  1623	            *(scheme for scheme, _ in view.has_top_concept),
  1624	        }
  1625	    )

  1628	def _select_publisher_view(view: PublisherView, subset: str) -> PublisherView:
  1629	    """Apply one narrow, source-declared partition selector to publisher claims."""
  1630	    if subset == "all":
  1631	        return view
  1632	    if subset not in {"eurovoc-main", "eurovoc-domains"}:
  1633	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported publisher subset selector: {subset}")
  1634	
  1635	    domain_scheme = "http://eurovoc.europa.eu/domains"
  1636	    domain_concepts = frozenset(subject for subject, target in view.memberships if target == domain_scheme)
  1637	    concepts = view.concepts - domain_concepts if subset == "eurovoc-main" else domain_concepts
  1638	    schemes = view.schemes - {domain_scheme} if subset == "eurovoc-main" else frozenset({domain_scheme})
  1639	    relations = frozenset(row for row in view.relations if row[0] in concepts)
  1640	    memberships = frozenset(row for row in view.memberships if row[0] in concepts)
  1641	    top_concept_of = frozenset(row for row in view.top_concept_of if row[0] in concepts)
  1642	    has_top_concept = frozenset(row for row in view.has_top_concept if row[1] in concepts)
  1643	    source_scheme_references = {
  1644	        *(scheme for _, scheme in memberships),
  1645	        *(scheme for _, scheme in top_concept_of),
  3670

  3672	def build_context(
  3673	    distribution: Path,
  3674	    source_root: Path,
  3675	    expectations: Expectations | None = None,
  3676	    specs: Sequence[SourceSpec] = SOURCES,
  3677	    scoped_out_specs: Sequence[SourceSpec] = (),
  3678	) -> Context:
  3679	    """Authenticate and read all declared inputs while collecting recoverable errors."""
  3680	    specs = tuple(specs)
  3681	    scoped_out_specs = tuple(scoped_out_specs)
  3682	    expectations = expectations or Expectations()
  3683	    summary_path = distribution / CONSTRUCTION_SUMMARY
  3684	    units: list[DistributionUnit] = []
  3685	    summary_digest: str | None = None
  3686	    manifest_digest: str | None = None
  3687	    pack_pins: dict[str, PackPin] = {}
  3688	    load_failures: list[str] = []
  3689	
  3690	    manifest_path = distribution / "atlas-manifest.json"
  3691	    if manifest_path.is_file():
  3692	        try:
  3693	            manifest_bytes = manifest_path.read_bytes()
  3694	            manifest_digest = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(manifest_bytes).hexdigest()
  3695	            manifest_payload = json.loads(manifest_bytes)
  3696	        except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
  3697	            load_failures.append(f"cannot read atlas-manifest.json: {error}")
  3698	        else:
  3699	            manifest_packs = (
  3700	                manifest_payload.get("packs") if isinstance(manifest_payload, dict) else None
  3701	            )
  3702	            if not isinstance(manifest_packs, list):
  3703	                load_failures.append("atlas-manifest.json: packs must be an array")
  3704	            else:
  3705	                for index, row in enumerate(manifest_packs):
  3706	                    try:
  3707	                        if not isinstance(row, dict):
  3708	                            raise TypeError("pack row must be an object")
  3709	                        path = row.get("path")
  3710	                        transport = row.get("transport")
  3711	                        if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.startswith("packs/"):
  3712	                            raise TypeError("path must be a packs/ relative string")
  3713	                        if not isinstance(transport, dict):
  3714	                            raise TypeError("transport must be an object")
  3715	                        digest = transport.get("digest")
  3716	                        byte_length = transport.get("byteLength")
  3717	                        if not isinstance(digest, str) or re.fullmatch(
  3718	                            r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", digest
  3719	                        ) is None:
  3720	                            raise TypeError("transport.digest must be a SHA-256")
  3721	                        if (
  3722	                            not isinstance(byte_length, int)
  3723	                            or isinstance(byte_length, bool)
  3724	                            or byte_length < 0
  3725	                        ):
  3726	                            raise TypeError("transport.byteLength must be a nonnegative integer")
  3727	                        logical_path = path.removeprefix("packs/")
  3728	                        if logical_path in pack_pins:
  3729	                            raise ValueError(f"duplicate manifest pack path {path!r}")
  3730	                        pack_pins[logical_path] = PackPin(
  3731	                            path=logical_path,
  3732	                            sha256=digest,
  3733	                            byte_length=byte_length,
  3734	                        )
  3735	                    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
  3736	                        load_failures.append(
  3737	                            f"atlas-manifest.json: packs[{index}]: {error}"
  3738	                        )
  3739	    elif expectations.require_pack_pins:
  3740	        load_failures.append("missing atlas-manifest.json for pack transport authentication")
  3741	
  3742	    if summary_path.is_file():
  3743	        try:
  3744	            summary_bytes = summary_path.read_bytes()
  3745	            summary_digest = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(summary_bytes).hexdigest()
  3746	            payload = json.loads(summary_bytes)
  3747	        except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
  3748	            load_failures.append(f"cannot read {CONSTRUCTION_SUMMARY}: {error}")
  3749	        else:
  3750	            releases = payload.get("releases") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
  3751	            if not isinstance(releases, list):
  3752	                load_failures.append(f"{CONSTRUCTION_SUMMARY}: releases must be an array")
  3753	            else:
  3754	                seen_keys: set[str] = set()
  3755	                for index, row in enumerate(releases):
  3756	                    try:
  3757	                        if not isinstance(row, dict):
  3758	                            raise TypeError("release row must be an object")
  3759	                        key = row["key"]
  3760	                        kind = row["kind"]
  3761	                        inputs = row.get("inputs", ())
  3762	                        rdf_packs = row.get("rdfPacks", ())
  3763	                        record_counts = row.get("recordCounts", {})
  3764	                        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
  3765	                            raise TypeError("key must be a non-empty string")
  3766	                        if key in seen_keys:
  3767	                            raise ValueError(f"duplicate construction unit key {key!r}")
  3768	                        if not isinstance(kind, str):
  3769	                            raise TypeError("kind must be a string")
  3770	                        if not isinstance(inputs, list) or not all(isinstance(item, dict) for item in inputs):
  3771	                            raise TypeError("inputs must be an array of objects")
  3772	                        if not isinstance(rdf_packs, list) or not all(
  3773	                            isinstance(item, dict) and isinstance(item.get("path"), str) for item in rdf_packs
  3774	                        ):
  3775	                            raise TypeError("rdfPacks must be an array of objects with string paths")
  3776	                        if not isinstance(record_counts, dict):
  3777	                            raise TypeError("recordCounts must be an object")
  3778	                        units.append(
  3779	                            DistributionUnit(
  3780	                                key=key,
  3781	                                kind=kind,
  3782	                                inputs=tuple(inputs),
  3783	                                packs=tuple(pack["path"].removeprefix("packs/") for pack in rdf_packs),
  3784	                                record_counts=record_counts,
  3785	                            )
  3786	                        )
  3787	                        seen_keys.add(key)
  3788	                    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
  3789	                        load_failures.append(f"{CONSTRUCTION_SUMMARY}: releases[{index}]: {error}")
  3790	    else:
  3791	        load_failures.append(f"missing {CONSTRUCTION_SUMMARY}")
  3792	    units_by_key = {unit.key: unit for unit in units}
  3793	
  3794	    verified_pins: set[SourcePin] = set()
  3795	    authenticated_payloads: dict[SourcePin, bytes] = {}
  3796	    pin_failures: list[str] = []
  3797	    for pin in dict.fromkeys(pin for spec in specs for pin in spec.inputs):
  3798	        try:
  3799	            authenticated_payloads[pin] = read_verified_file_pin(
  3800	                _resolve_source_pin(source_root, pin),
  3801	                expected_sha256=pin.sha256,
  3802	                expected_byte_length=pin.byte_length,
  3803	                logical_path=pin.path,
  3804	            )
  3805	        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - authenticate every other declared input
  3806	            pin_failures.append(f"{pin.path}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
  3807	        else:
  3808	            verified_pins.add(pin)
  3809	
  3810	    pairs: list[SourcePair] = []
  3811	    native_control_pairs: list[NativeControlPair] = []
  3812	    source_extract_pairs: list[SourceExtractPair] = []
  3813	    atlas_views: list[tuple[SourceSpec, AtlasView]] = []
  3814	    publisher_cache: dict[
  3815	        tuple[tuple[SourcePin, ...], tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]],
  3816	        PublisherView | str,
  3817	    ] = {}
  3818	    native_specs = [spec for spec in specs if spec.kind == "native-control"]
  3819	    native_control_publishers: dict[SourceSpec, NativeControlPublisherView] = {}
  3820	    if native_specs:
  3821	        try:
  3822	            native_control_publishers, native_control_load_failures = (
  3823	                _read_native_control_publishers(native_specs, authenticated_payloads)
  3824	            )
  3825	        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - RDF comparisons must still run
  3826	            load_failures.extend(
  3827	                f"{spec.name}: native source reader failed: {type(error).__name__}: {error}"
  3828	                for spec in native_specs
  3829	            )
  3830	        else:
  3831	            load_failures.extend(native_control_load_failures)
  3832	    for spec in specs:
  3833	        packs = tuple(
  3834	            pack
  3835	            for release_key in spec.release_keys
  3836	            for pack in units_by_key.get(
  3837	                release_key,
  3838	                DistributionUnit(release_key, "missing", (), (), {}),
  3839	            ).packs
  3840	        )
  3841	        publisher: PublisherView | None = None
  3842	        if spec.kind in RDF_COMPARISON_KINDS:
  3843	            additional_annotation_predicates = (
  3844	                spec.rdf_source.additional_annotation_predicates
  3845	                if spec.rdf_source is not None
  3846	                else ()
  3847	            )
  3848	            additional_relation_predicates = (
  3849	                spec.rdf_source.additional_relation_predicates
  3850	                if spec.rdf_source is not None
  3851	                else ()
  3852	            )
  3853	            cache_key = (
  3854	                spec.inputs,
  3855	                additional_annotation_predicates,
  3856	                additional_relation_predicates,
  3857	                # Two comparisons can share the same pinned bytes and declare
  3858	                # different scopes (EuroVoc main and domains do), so the
  3859	                # declarations belong in the key: a cached view built under one
  3860	                # spec's exclusions is not the other's view.
  3861	                spec.declared_claim_exclusions,
  3862	            )
  3863	            cached = publisher_cache.get(cache_key)
  3864	            if cached is None:
  3865	                try:
  3866	                    cached = _read_publisher_pin_set(
  3867	                        spec.inputs,
  3868	                        " + ".join(sorted(pin.path for pin in spec.inputs)),
  3869	                        authenticated_payloads,
  3870	                        additional_annotation_predicates=(
  3871	                            additional_annotation_predicates
  3872	                        ),
  3873	                        additional_relation_predicates=additional_relation_predicates,
  3874	                        declared_claim_exclusions=spec.declared_claim_exclusions,
  3875	                    )
  3876	                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep reading independent sources
  3877	                    cached = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
  3878	                publisher_cache[cache_key] = cached
  3879	            if isinstance(cached, str):
  3880	                load_failures.append(f"{spec.name}: publisher inputs could not be read: {cached}")
  3881	            else:
  3882	                try:
  3883	                    selected_publisher = _select_publisher_view(cached, spec.subset)
  3884	                    selected_publisher = _select_publisher_concepts(
  3885	                        selected_publisher,
  3886	                        spec.included_concept_iris,
  3887	                    )
  3888	                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - continue with every later source
  3889	                    load_failures.append(
  3890	                        f"{spec.name}: publisher comparison scope could not be selected: "
  3891	                        f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
  3892	                    )
  3893	                else:
  3894	                    publisher = selected_publisher
  3895	
  3896	        source_claim_subjects = (
  3897	            frozenset(
  3898	                {
  3899	                    *publisher.concepts,
  3900	                    *_publisher_source_scheme_subjects(publisher),
  3901	                    *publisher.resource_annotation_target_claim_counts,
  3902	                    *(subject for subject, _, _ in publisher.relations),
  3903	                    *(obj for _, _, obj in publisher.relations),
  3904	                }
  3905	            )
  3906	            if publisher is not None
  3907	            else frozenset()
  3908	        )
  3909	        try:
  3910	            atlas = read_atlas_source(
  3911	                distribution,
  3912	                packs,
  3913	                source_claim_subjects,
  3914	            )
  3915	        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - continue with every later source
  3916	            load_failures.append(

  1628	def _select_publisher_view(view: PublisherView, subset: str) -> PublisherView:
  1629	    """Apply one narrow, source-declared partition selector to publisher claims."""
  1630	    if subset == "all":
  1631	        return view
  1632	    if subset not in {"eurovoc-main", "eurovoc-domains"}:

  1638	    schemes = view.schemes - {domain_scheme} if subset == "eurovoc-main" else frozenset({domain_scheme})

codex
The adapter asymmetry is now verified: OSTI, ELSST, and GEMET populate `RegistryResource.definition`/`notes`; EuroVoc, AGROVOC, bounded NALT, and NASA do not. EuroVoc is especially revealing because its parser/claim release retains the source claims, but the final resource-selection rules select only labels, notations, and structural IRIs. I’m measuring the exact audit scopes next, including English-eligible text separately from all publisher claims so the owner can see what “carry English” still leaves to declare.

def _english(language_tag: str | None, *, untagged_is_english: bool = False) -> bool:
    if language_tag is None:
        return untagged_is_english
    return language_tag.casefold() == "en"


def _literal_payload(value: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    payload = {
        "value": value.lexical_form,
    }
    if value.language_tag is not None:
        if not _english(value.language_tag):
            raise ValueError("non-English literal cannot enter an Atlas native payload")
        payload["language"] = "en"
    if value.datatype_iri is not None:
        payload["datatypeIri"] = value.datatype_iri
    return payload

def read_pack(
    path: Path,
    failures: list[str] | None = None,
    observations: dict[str, tuple[str, int]] | None = None,
    logical_path: str | None = None,
) -> Iterator[Quad]:
    """Parse one immutable pack snapshot and retain its actual transport identity."""
    payload = path.read_bytes()
    if observations is not None:
        observations[logical_path or path.as_posix()] = (
            "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
            len(payload),
        )
    with zstd.open(io.BytesIO(payload), "rt", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for number, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
            try:
                quad = parse_nquads_line(line)
            except ValueError as error:
                detail = f"{path.name}:{number}: {error}"
                if failures is None:
                    raise ValueError(detail) from error
                failures.append(detail)
                continue
            if quad is not None:
                yield quad

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LiteralValue:
    """One literal with the language and datatype needed to detect silent rewrites."""

    value: str
    language: str | None
    datatype: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReifiedStatement:
    """One exact RDF reification row from publisher bytes."""

    statement_iri: str
    subject_iri: str
    predicate_iri: str
    object_iri: str | None = None
    object_literal: LiteralValue | None = None


def _literal_value(value: str, language: str | None, datatype: str | None) -> LiteralValue:
    """Represent the RDF 1.1 datatype of a plain literal explicitly."""
    if language is None and datatype is None:
        datatype = f"{XSD}string"
    return LiteralValue(value, language, datatype)


def _literal_repr(literal: LiteralValue) -> str:
    """Render one literal with the tag or datatype that makes a rewrite visible."""
    if literal.language is not None:
        return f"{literal.value!r}@{literal.language}"
    return f"{literal.value!r}^^<{literal.datatype}>"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SourceExtractSelector:
    """One non-RDF publisher artifact compared through its checked-in extract.

    Some publishers ship no machine-readable distribution at all -- the Federal
    Register thesaurus is a styled PDF. For those releases the comparison basis
    is the repository-checked semantic extract of the pinned artifact: bytes
    that live in git, are pinned here by digest, are *not* read by the builder
    (which re-parses the PDF on every build), and whose own header binds the
    exact publisher artifact this comparison authenticates.

    This is weaker than the RDF comparisons and says so in the receipt: it is
    not an independent re-parse of the publisher's bytes, it is a frozen
    re-statement of them. What it does catch is every drift between what the
    builder parsed out of the pinned artifact and what git recorded.
    """

    reader: str
    extract: SourcePin
    source_release_iri: str
    label_language: str
    relation_predicate: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DeclaredClaimExclusion:
    """One publisher entity layer a release declares Atlas does not represent.

    This is a claim-scope declaration, never a waiver. Some publishers ship
    entity kinds beside their terms -- GEMET's Group/Theme/SuperGroup
    collections and its bibliographic Source register, the Publications Office's
    void/lime dataset descriptions -- that Atlas deliberately does not model.
    Leaving those claims in the uncovered report says "we have not looked yet",
    which is false; dropping them silently is worse. An exclusion says instead:
    here is the exact subject set, here is every claim it covers counted by
    predicate, and here is the paired assertion that Atlas asserts *nothing*
    about any of those subjects.

    That pairing is what keeps it fail-closed. The exclusion only ever removes
    publisher claims from the residue; the Atlas side of the same subjects stays
    in the comparison, so one manufactured claim about an excluded subject fails
    both ``source-claim-coverage`` and ``claim-scope``. An exclusion that
    overlaps a subject the comparison actually compares is itself a failure.

    Subjects are selected by declared rdf:type or by IRI prefix -- both
    enumerable from the publisher's own bytes, so the receipt can print the set.
    """

    name: str
    reason: str
    subject_types: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    subject_iri_prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.subject_types and not self.subject_iri_prefixes:
            raise ValueError(
                f"declared claim exclusion {self.name!r} selects no subjects; an "
                "exclusion must name the exact subject set it covers"
            )

    def selects(self, subject: str, types: frozenset[str]) -> bool:
        """Return whether one publisher subject falls inside this declaration."""
        if self.subject_types & types:
            return True
        return bool(self.subject_iri_prefixes) and subject.startswith(
            self.subject_iri_prefixes
        )

"""Independent source-fidelity verifier for a packed RefSpec Atlas 3.1 distribution.

The eleven acceptance gates recorded in ``atlas-acceptance.json`` prove that a
distribution is internally consistent: canonical JSON, schema conformance, SHACL
conformance, referential closure, projection determinism, reasoner isolation, and
a ledger that reconciles with the graph it was written from. Every one of those
gates reads only the built artifact. None of them opens the pinned publisher
bytes. A build that read every publisher file, transcribed every label wrong, and
then wrote a self-consistent ledger would pass all eleven with ``verdict: passed``.

This verifier closes that gap from the other side. It parses the pinned
publisher bytes with stock format libraries, streams what the Atlas actually
asserts out of the distribution packs, and compares the two directly. It imports
no RefSpec semantic reader, builder, or normalisation code because a defect in
ingestion would be reproduced identically by any check written from the same
code, and the two would agree. It shares only the transformation-free file-pin
helper used to authenticate bytes. Agreement between a program and its own
reflection is not evidence.

The comparison includes only claims attributable to publisher inputs. Atlas-owned
release nodes, semantic rings, resource profiles, governed schemes, and class
assignments are outside its scope. The Atlas binding validator checks those
Atlas-specific structures separately; this command does not run or report it.

Two load-bearing facts about the join, stated here so they are not silently
rediscovered:

* An Atlas resource for a vocabulary source **is** the publisher's own IRI. The
  data join is IRI identity, not a minted key and not a digest. Source locators
  are adapter-specific evidence addresses and are checked independently. The one
  exception is a ``source-extract`` comparison, where the publisher ships no IRIs
  at all: there the join is the source-local identity the Atlas record itself
  declares in ``atlas:nativePayload``, and the comparison says so in the receipt.
* ``atlas:sourceDigest`` is source-specific: some adapters retain a publisher
  file or archive-member digest, while others digest a constructed native
  relation. The verifier checks the applicable digest rule, but never treats a
  matching digest as a substitute for field-level comparison.

Findings are separated by who owns them. A ``source`` finding is a defect in the
publisher's own data; preserving it faithfully is correct behaviour and it never
fails the run. A ``pipeline`` finding is a difference between the publisher bytes
and what we assert about them, and it fails the run. Narrow executable policies
may define an Atlas representation only after checking their exact prerequisites
and exact permitted claim set; a policy name is never a waiver.

Usage. ``--distribution`` is required: there is no default distribution, because
a default silently audits whatever build happens to be on disk (the retired
``output/atlas-3.0-full-2026-08-07-ring-audit`` tree was exactly that). Name the
artifact, or go through the Makefile target, which names it for you::

    make audit-atlas-v3-source-fidelity \\
        ATLAS_V3_AUDIT_ROOT=output/atlas-3.1-federal-register-thesaurus-2025-04-01

    uv run python tools/verify_atlas_source_fidelity.py \\
        --distribution output/atlas-3.1-federal-register-thesaurus-2025-04-01/distribution \\
        --output findings.json

``--only NAME`` (repeatable) restricts the run to named comparisons, so a bounded
artifact costs a bounded run. It narrows what is proven, never what is claimed:
construction units owned by the comparisons left out are reported as *not
evaluated (scoped out)*, never as covered and never as failed, and the receipt
names every comparison the run skipped. Within the scope both directions still
fail closed.

Exit codes: ``0`` all checks passed and ``1`` one or more checks failed. Missing
or malformed inputs are collected as check failures so the remaining independent
inputs and checks still run.
"""

def _is_atlas_representation_iri(iri: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether an IRI is minted in a namespace Atlas itself owns."""
    return iri.startswith(ATLAS_REPRESENTATION_NAMESPACES)

def read_publisher_skos(path: Path, fmt: str, source: str, zip_member: str | None = None) -> PublisherView:
    """Read one pinned SKOS distribution into the comparison form."""
    return _publisher_view(_load_graph(path, fmt, zip_member), source)


def _resolve_source_pin(source_root: Path, pin: SourcePin) -> Path:
    """Resolve a declared input without allowing it to escape the two approved roots."""
    candidates = (source_root / pin.path, REPOSITORY_ROOT / pin.path)
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.is_file() and not candidate.is_symlink():
            return candidate
    return candidates[0]


def _read_publisher_pin_set(
    inputs: Sequence[SourcePin],
    source: str,
    authenticated_payloads: Mapping[SourcePin, bytes],
    *,
    additional_annotation_predicates: Sequence[str] = (),
    additional_relation_predicates: Sequence[str] = (),
    declared_claim_exclusions: Sequence[DeclaredClaimExclusion] = (),
) -> PublisherView:
    """Read all RDF inputs, reporting every unreadable member before failing the set."""
    import rdflib

    graph = rdflib.Graph()
    failures: list[str] = []
    resource_input_digests: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    input_content_digests: dict[str, str] = {}
    for pin in inputs:
        try:
            payload = authenticated_payloads[pin]
            loaded = _load_graph_payload(
                payload,
                pin.fmt,
                pin.zip_member,
                public_id=pin.source_iri,
            )
            content = payload
            if pin.zip_member is not None:
                with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(payload)) as archive:
                    content = archive.read(pin.zip_member)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - inspect the remaining declared inputs
            failures.append(f"{pin.path}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
            continue
        content_digest = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
        input_content_digests[pin.path] = content_digest
        for subject in loaded.subjects():
            if isinstance(subject, rdflib.URIRef):
                resource_input_digests[str(subject)].add(content_digest)
        graph += loaded
        for prefix, namespace in loaded.namespaces():
            graph.bind(prefix, namespace, replace=True)
    if failures:
        raise ValueError("; ".join(failures))
    return _publisher_view(
        graph,
        source,
        additional_annotation_predicates=additional_annotation_predicates,
        additional_relation_predicates=additional_relation_predicates,
        resource_input_digests={
            resource: frozenset(digests)
            for resource, digests in resource_input_digests.items()
        },
        input_content_digests=input_content_digests,
        declared_claim_exclusions=declared_claim_exclusions,
    )


def read_publisher_inputs(source_root: Path, spec: SourceSpec) -> PublisherView:
    """Read and union every independently pinned RDF input for one comparison scope."""
    payloads = {
        pin: read_verified_file_pin(
            _resolve_source_pin(source_root, pin),
            expected_sha256=pin.sha256,
            expected_byte_length=pin.byte_length,
            logical_path=pin.path,
        )
        for pin in spec.inputs
    }
    view = _select_publisher_view(
        _read_publisher_pin_set(
            spec.inputs,
            spec.name,
            payloads,
            additional_annotation_predicates=(
                spec.rdf_source.additional_annotation_predicates
                if spec.rdf_source is not None
                else ()
            ),
            additional_relation_predicates=(
                spec.rdf_source.additional_relation_predicates
                if spec.rdf_source is not None
                else ()
            ),
            declared_claim_exclusions=spec.declared_claim_exclusions,
        ),
        spec.subset,
    )
    return _select_publisher_concepts(view, spec.included_concept_iris)

            *view.schemes,
            *(scheme for _, scheme in view.memberships),
            *(scheme for _, scheme in view.top_concept_of),
            *(scheme for scheme, _ in view.has_top_concept),
        }
    )

def ntriples_term(term: Any) -> str:
    """Render one RDF term in one deterministic RDF 1.1 N-Triples form."""

    try:
        return _cached_iri_term(term) if isinstance(term, URIRef) else _canonical_ntriples_term(term)
    except RdfCanonicalError as exc:
        code = "rdf.blank-node" if isinstance(term, BNode) else "rdf.term"
        _fail(code, str(exc))


def nquads_line(
    subject: URIRef,
    predicate: URIRef,
    obj: URIRef | Literal,
    graph_id: URIRef,
) -> str:
    """Render one canonical named-graph RDF 1.1 N-Quads statement."""

    return " ".join(
        (
            ntriples_term(subject),
            ntriples_term(predicate),
            ntriples_term(obj),
            ntriples_term(graph_id),
            ".",
        )
    )


def _canonical_dataset_lines(
    dataset: Dataset,
    *,
    blank_node_code: str,
    blank_node_detail: str,
) -> list[str]:
    """Render parsed quads canonically while rejecting actual blank-node terms."""

    lines: list[str] = []

        if any(isinstance(term, BNode) for term in (subject, predicate, obj, graph_id)):
            _fail(blank_node_code, blank_node_detail)

"""Compact an authenticated Atlas Parquet view for search and graph browsing.

The compact view preserves graph facts, labels, statement provenance, source
locators, and stable identifiers. It replaces repeated references with
deterministic 32-byte keys and omits only source-native payload bodies. The
full logical-record view and canonical RDF remain the audit sources.
"""

class AtlasParquetSearchViewError(ValueError):
    """The full view or compact search view is unsafe or inconsistent."""


def _safe_member_path(directory: Path, relative: object) -> Path:
    if not isinstance(relative, str):
        raise AtlasParquetSearchViewError("compact view member path must be text")
    parsed = PurePosixPath(relative)
    if parsed.is_absolute() or not parsed.parts or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in parsed.parts):
        raise AtlasParquetSearchViewError(f"compact view member path is unsafe: {relative!r}")
    return directory.joinpath(*parsed.parts)


def _suffix(value: str | None, prefix_name: str) -> bytes | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    prefix = _PREFIXES[prefix_name]
    if not value.startswith(prefix):
        raise AtlasParquetSearchViewError(f"{prefix_name} identifier has an unsupported prefix: {value}")
    suffix = value.removeprefix(prefix)
    if len(suffix) != 64:
        raise AtlasParquetSearchViewError(f"{prefix_name} identifier has an unsupported digest suffix")
    try:
        return bytes.fromhex(suffix)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise AtlasParquetSearchViewError(f"{prefix_name} identifier has a non-hex digest suffix") from error


_B32 = pa.binary(32)
_SCHEMAS: Mapping[CompactRecordRole, pa.Schema] = {
    CompactRecordRole.RESOURCE: pa.schema(
        [

            pa.field("release", pa.string(), nullable=False),
